Josh scowled from across the circle, his bruised face still evident from their sparring match. "So, we're just supposed to hand them over to HQ? Why not keep some for ourselves? We could use them to power up our shelter, maybe even our weapons."
Tess sighed but kept her tone measured. "HQ's resources are stretched thin. These crystals could make a huge difference in the larger fight against the Dragon Emperor. We're part of something bigger, Josh. Remember that."
Josh muttered something under his breath, but he didn't argue further.
Tess turned her gaze to Rey. "The rendezvous point and date will be set by HQ. They'll contact us in the next few days, but only a small team will go for the delivery. In the meantime, Rey, I think it's time we addressed your situation."
Rey arched an eyebrow, playing coy. "My situation?"
"You need to get stronger," Tess said bluntly. "You've proven you're skilled, no question there. But your ability is… unique, and we don't know its limits. The best way to understand it is to see it in action—against Monsters."
A murmur rippled through the group. Josh's scowl deepened, but others, like Mina and Felix, nodded in agreement.
Rey's face remained neutral, but inside, he was grinning.
This was exactly what he wanted: an opportunity to fight, to grow stronger by leveling up. While everyone was still trying to understand the limits of [Doppel], he would use the opportunity to rack up Stat Points and Levels.
"I'm on board," Rey said, his tone calm and confident. "When do we start?"
"Tomorrow," Tess replied. "We'll take you to an area not too far from here. It's crawling with Monsters, but nothing we can't handle together. Consider it a trial run."
"Together?" Rey asked, genuinely curious.
"Of course," Tess said, smiling faintly. "You're part of the Resistance now, Rey. We don't throw people to the wolves. Not even if they have lightning coursing through their veins."
The group chuckled lightly at her comment, breaking some of the tension in the room. Josh, however, remained silent, his eyes fixed on Rey with an intensity that promised this wasn't over.
Later that evening, as the group prepared for the next day's excursion, Tess approached Rey in his room. She leaned against the doorway, watching him as he sharpened a blade he'd borrowed from their armory.
"You seem… eager," Tess said, folding her arms.
"Shouldn't I be?" Rey replied without looking up. "You're giving me the chance to prove myself—and to get stronger. I'd be an idiot not to take it seriously."
Tess studied him for a moment before stepping inside. "Most people would be nervous about facing Monsters for the first time."
Rey glanced up at her, a faint smirk tugging at his lips. "Who says it's my first time?"
Tess raised an eyebrow.
"I mean, the fact that I have this power, and my body seems to know how it works means I must have awakened at some point… even though I can't remember the details." He added. "I could have fought Monsters, maybe even been part of some other Resistance or Shelter."
"Yeah… maybe."
"Besides, I have you all with me, with your powers too. Monsters should just be like lager animals, right? Shouldn't be too hard."
"Fair point. But this is different. These Monsters aren't mindless beasts—they're corrupted by the Dragon Emperor's power. They're smarter, stronger, and more dangerous than anything you're thinking about."
"I'll manage," Rey said confidently.
"I hope so," Tess replied. "Because if you can't, you're putting all of us at risk."
Her words hung in the air, heavy with implication.
Rey met her gaze, unflinching. "I won't let you down."
Tess nodded, her expression softening slightly.
"See that you don't."
********
The next morning, the group set out at dawn.
The world outside the shelter was bleak and unforgiving, the sky a perpetual shade of gray that made it hard to tell where the horizon ended and the heavens began. The landscape was a twisted parody of what Earth once was, with jagged, blackened trees and rivers of stagnant, dark water.
Rey walked near the front of the group, his senses sharp. Tess led the way, her movements swift and precise, while Josh lingered at the back, his eyes darting between Rey and the surrounding terrain.
They reached the edge of a sprawling, desolate plain, where the ground was cracked and scorched, and the air felt charged with a strange, unnatural energy.
"This is the spot," Tess said, stopping abruptly.
She turned to face the group. "Stay sharp. We'll move as a unit and watch each other's backs. Rey, stick close to me until we get a sense of what's out here."
Rey nodded, his expression serious.
"Understood."

chapters.title: Chapter 919: Rey Vs Monsters
chapters.content:
Chapter 919: Rey Vs Monsters
The group advanced cautiously, their weapons at the ready.
The silence was oppressive, broken only by the sound of their footsteps crunching against the brittle earth.
Then, without warning, the ground ahead of them erupted.
"GROOOOAHHH!!!"
Three hulking, misshapen creatures emerged, their bodies a grotesque amalgamation of flesh, bone, and what looked like molten metal. Their eyes glowed with an eerie, crimson light, and they let out guttural, inhuman roars that echoed across the plain.
Rey's heart raced, but he forced himself to stay calm.
'Damn... I'm missing some of my old skills right now.'
Tess barked orders, and the group moved into formation, each member preparing to engage.
"Rey," Tess called, her voice steady despite the chaos. "This is your chance. Show us what you can do."
Rey nodded, stepping forward as the first Monster charged toward him.
He focused intently, his [Doppel] ability activating as he analyzed the creature's movements.
'Let's see what you've got,' Rey thought, a determined grin spreading across his face as he prepared to fight. 'I hope you have some nice skills... but even if you don't I'm sure you have those nice EXP to spare!'
~WHOOOOSH!~
The first Monster lunged at Rey with molten-metal claws poised to tear him apart.
He activated [High Sense], heightening his awareness of its every movement. As the claws swung toward his torso, he countered with [Space-Shift], vanishing from its path and reappearing behind its lumbering form.
Without hesitation, he slammed a stone-encased fist-powered by [Stone Transformation] -into the back of the Monster's head.
~BAM!~
The impact sent it sprawling to the ground, molten sparks flying from its cracked skull.
A second Monster roared and charged at Rey's exposed flank.
Reacting instantly, he threw up a shimmering (Light Shield].
The creature's claws raked across the barrier, causing it to flicker and buckle, but it held just long enough for him to leap back. Extending a hand, Rey summoned moisture from the air using [Moist Meter], whipping it into a dense jet of water that struck the Monster square in its glowing eyes, eliciting a screech of pain.
The third Monster flanked him from the other side.
Planting his feet, Rey focused his energy as electricity crackled around his body. Activating [Electrical Surge], he cloaked himself in a deadly current that caused the creature to hesitate, its instincts warning it of danger.
Rey didn't wait.
Using a burst of speed fueled by [Physical Enhancement], he tackled the Monster head-on, slamming electrified fists into its chest.
The creature convulsed and collapsed to the ground, twitching from the residual charge.
Rey barely had time to breathe before the first Monster recovered, dazed but relentless, and lunged again.
He sidestepped with [Space-Shift], reappearing midair above it, and unleashed a concussive [Soundwave]. The force rattled the ground and caused the Monster to stumble, its molten- metal body vibrating uncontrollably.
Taking advantage of its disorientation, Rey extended his shadow with [Shadow Control], dark tendrils wrapping around the creature's limbs to immobilize it. A thunderous punch with his stone-covered fist shattered its skull, silencing it for good.
"GRRRIIKKKK!"
The second Monster, still thrashing from the water assault, recovered and lunged at him with renewed ferocity.
Rey shifted tactics, activating [Camouflage] to blend seamlessly into the ashen landscape. The creature screeched, its glowing eyes scanning the area in confusion.
Rey reappeared behind it, silently manipulating his shadow into a spiked construct.
With a sharp motion, the shadow spear drove through the Monster's back, ending its rampage.
~SQUELCH!~
The final Monster, still sparking from its earlier encounter with Rey's electricity, attempted
to retreat.
He wouldn't allow it.
Summoning the last remnants of moisture from the dry air, Rey condensed it into a blade of water and hurled it at the creature's neck.
The weapon struck true, slicing through its molten flesh and dropping the Monster with a gurgling roar.
Rey had little time to recover before the ground trembled anew.
A dozen more Monsters emerged from the desolate plain, their guttural growls reverberating
as they surrounded him. His team called out from the edge of the battlefield, but Rey raised a hand, signaling them to stay back.
"I've got this," he said, his voice firm despite his exhaustion.
The new wave attacked with relentless fury.
Rey activated [High Sense] once more, his heightened awareness turning the battlefield into a blur of potential threats and opportunities.
The first Monster lunged, and he retaliated with a bolt of lightning from [Electrical Surge], striking the molten creature through its core.
~TZZZTZ!~
Two more charged at him, but he evaded with [Space-Shift], reappearing above them to slam his stone-encased fists into their skulls, leaving them crumpled in the dirt.
A larger Monster roared and spat molten projectiles toward him.
Rey threw up his [Light Shield], but the molten shards pierced through, searing his arm.
"Gahhh!"
Gritting his teeth against the pain, he retaliated with a deafening [Soundwave], sending the creature staggering back. He followed up by extending his shadow, forming spikes and tendrils with [Shadow Control] that impaled and restrained three more Monsters at once.
The chaos continued as Rey cycled through his skills with precision.
When another Monster flanked him, he activated [Camouflage] to vanish, reappearing behind it to deliver a decisive blow. A charging Monster found its footing undone as Rey summoned water with [Moist Meter], freezing it into a slick sheet that caused the creature to skid uncontrollably into a nearby boulder.
The final two Monsters attacked together, their molten claws slashing with lethal intent.
Rey dodged one with [Space-Shift] and faced the other head-on, channeling all his strength through [Physical Enhancement].
Letting out a fierce roar, he drove his fist through the creature's chest, then spun around to hurl a bolt of lightning at the last Monster.
~BOOM!~
It fell with a smoldering thud, and the battlefield finally fell silent.
"Haaa... haaa..."
Rey stood in the center of the carnage, panting heavily, his body trembling from exertion. Blood-both his and the Monsters'-covered him, streaking his clothes and pooling at his feet. He turned to his team, who stared at him in stunned silence, their expressions a mix of
awe and disbelief.
A weary but triumphant smile crossed Rey's face as he met Tess's wide-eyed gaze.
"What's next?"

chapters.title: Chapter 920: The Nest
chapters.content:
Chapter 920: The Nest
"REY!"
The adrenaline still coursed through Rey's body as the team approached him cautiously, their eyes scanning the battlefield littered with fallen Monsters. Tess stepped forward first, her sharp gaze softening as she noted the blood dripping from his numerous cuts and bruises.
"You're a mess," she said, her tone a mix of concern and admiration.
Rey smirked, brushing off her words even as his legs trembled beneath him.
"I'm fine. Really."
"You don't look fine," Josh quipped, but the usual edge in his voice was absent. He scratched the back of his head awkwardly. "Still... that was pretty cool."
The unexpected praise made Rey glance at him, a raised eyebrow hinting at his surprise.
Josh rolled his eyes and added, "Don't make me say it again."
Tess pulled out a small vial filled with a glowing green liquid and handed it to Rey. "Drink this. It's a Health Brew. It'll patch you up."
Rey hesitated for a moment, then uncorked the vial and downed the potion in one gulp.
The cool, tingling sensation spread through his body, knitting his wounds and dulling the pain in his muscles.
"Haaa..."
He let out a relieved sigh as the restorative effects kicked in.
"Thanks," he said, flexing his fingers to test his recovery.
The others gathered around, each offering their thoughts.
"I've never seen anyone fight like that," Mei said, her voice filled with genuine awe.
"You took out all of them on your own," Isaac added. "That's insane."
Even Tess nodded, her arms crossed. "I hate to admit it this much, but you're impressive, Rey. You handled yourself well."
Rey grinned, the praise fueling his confidence. "So, what's next?"
Tess shook her head. "What's next is rest. You've done enough for now."
But Rey wasn't ready to stop.
"Come on, I can handle more. I feel great!" He gestured to the empty vial, as if the potion had made him invincible.
The group exchanged wary glances, and Tess sighed deeply.
"Rey-"
"If it's too dangerous, I'll retreat," he interrupted, his voice urgent. "I promise. I just need to keep fighting. I need to get stronger."
Her expression softened, and after a moment's pause, she relented.
"Fine. But under one condition-you don't enter the Nest."
"Nest?" Rey asked, his interest piqued.
"It's where Monsters gather in large numbers, usually protected by sentinels and ruled by a King," Tess explained. "The scouts you fought are nothing compared to what's inside. The sentinels are tougher, and a King is... well, let's just say it's on a whole different level."
Rey nodded eagerly. "Got it. I'll stay outside the Nest."
Tess studied him for a moment, then motioned for the group to move out.
"Alright, let's go."
The journey to the Monster Nest wasn't long, and as they climbed a rocky hill overlooking the area, Rey's eyes widened.
Below them lay a sprawling crater, jagged with darkened rocks and glowing faintly with strange energy. Dozens of Monsters roamed the outskirts, their hulking forms casting ominous shadows across the terrain.
Rey's lips curled into a smile, the sight igniting a fire within him.
This was the perfect place to grow stronger.
From the vantage point, he called out his [Status Window], watching as the translucent screen appeared before him.
[STATUS WINDOW]
- Name: Rey Skylar
- Race: Human
- Class: NIL
- Level: 10 (0.00% EXP)
- Life Force: 10
- Mana Level: 25
- Combat Ability: 15
- Stat Points: 10
- Skills (Exclusive): [Doppel]
- Skills (Non-Exclusive): NIL
- Alignment: Chaotic Neutral
[Additional Information]
Unknown... no information has been provided.
[End Of Information]
His Stats had improved significantly, and the sheer volume of Monsters he had defeated earlier had propelled him up several Levels.
'Most importantly, since my skills are all low-tier, I don't require a lot of Mana. In fact, it doesn't even seem like a lot of these skills take up any Mana at all. It's not even in their
description.'
And, everytime he fought and used his skills, he was automatically improving all of his Stats -even without spending any Stat Point.
'It won't be long before I get my first Non-Exclusive Skills, and once that happens, it'll only increase the speed at which I can get stronger.
He closed the window with a flick of his hand, his grin widening as he stared down at his foes. The sight of the Monster Nest sprawling below him like a scene from a nightmare. Dozens of creatures moved within the eerie glow of the crater, their forms hunched and grotesque. He tightened his fists, adrenaline coursing through his veins as he prepared to descend.
"This is going to be fun."
"Rey, remember what I said!" Tess called from above, her voice carrying a sharp edge.
"I'll stay outside," he reassured her, though his grin betrayed the excitement he felt. Without waiting for a response, Rey leapt down the slope, his body cutting through the air as he activated [Stone Transformation] mid-fall.
~WHUUM!~
He quickened his descent.
His body hardened into rock just before landing with an earth-shaking impact, scattering debris and startling the nearest Monsters.
~BOOM!~
The creatures turned toward him, their glowing eyes narrowing as they recognized the intruder. They were massive, their clawed limbs and jagged teeth gleaming in the faint light.
Rey counted over twenty closing in on him.
"Time to get to work," he muttered, his grin widening.
~WHOOSH!~
The first wave of Monsters lunged at him with deafening roars. Rey shifted seamlessly into [Camouflage], his form blending into the rocky terrain and confusing the charging beasts.
As the nearest one stumbled past, he struck, channeling [Physical Enhancement] to deliver a devastating punch that sent the creature hurtling into its companions.
Electricity crackled around him as he activated [Electrical Surge], arcs of lightning snapping through the air and striking multiple foes at once. The Monsters howled in pain, their charred forms collapsing to the ground.
One beast attempted to flank him, but Rey was faster.
He used [Space-Shift], closing the gap in an instant and driving his stone-like fist into the creature's skull. Another came from behind, and Rey countered with [Soundwave], releasing a concussive blast that knocked it off its feet.
But the sheer number of Monsters began to press him.
Clawed hands raked across his arm, leaving deep gashes, and another tackled him, forcing
him to the ground. Rey gritted his teeth, activating [Shadow Control] to bind his attackers
with tendrils of darkness.
He rolled to his feet, his movements fluid despite the pain, and finished the bound Monsters
with a surge of electricity.
"Come on!" he roared, his bloodied form defiant as more creatures swarmed him.
Switching tactics, Rey summoned a stream of water using [Moist Meter], weaving it around
him like a whip. The liquid cut through the air with deadly precision, slicing through the hide
of several Monsters.
When they recoiled, he followed up with [Light Shield], blocking a barrage of claws and teeth.
One particularly large beast lunged, its claws aimed for his throat.
Rey ducked and retaliated with [High Sense], his heightened perception allowing him to anticipate its movements. He sidestepped and drove an electrified punch into its chest, the force of the blow sending it crashing into a group of smaller Monsters.
"Haa... this is bothersome." He mumbled.
For every creature he defeated, two more seemed to take its place.
'None of my current skills have enough destructive power to one-shot these guys, and I don't have an area-of-effect ability that will do the trick."
That left him stuck fighting with the small fry, even struggling against their numbers.
If only his H'Trae self could see him now...
'One [Divine Ray] would have been more than enough...' He sighed. 'Well, it's too late to think
about that now.'
He simply had to make do with what he had.
~WHISH!~
The claws and teeth of the Monsters found their mark on occasion, leaving his body riddled
with cuts and bruises.
"Tch!" The pain wasn't dulled, so he felt the raw stings.
Yet, Rey fought on, holding steady thanks to the efficient energy consumption of his skills,
though his stamina was rapidly declining.
Minutes stretched into what felt like hours, and the ground was soon littered with the corpses
of defeated Monsters. Rey stood amidst the carnage, his chest heaving and his body covered in blood-some his own, most not.
"Haa.... haaaaa... is that al-?"
"RO00000000AAAAAAARRRRR!!!"
Before he could catch his breath, a guttural roar echoed from within the Nest. The sound was
deafening, shaking the very ground beneath his feet.
The team shouted from the ridge.
"Rey! Get out of there!" He turned to see them waving frantically, but his attention was drawn back to the Nest as its
shadowy entrance darkened further.
~RUMBLE!~
The earth shook.
Emerging from within was a massive creature, easily three times the size of the others.
Its body was covered in thick, obsidian-like scales, and its glowing red eyes radiated malevolence. Behind it came more Monsters, sentinels guarding their King.
The sheer size and number of them made Rey's confidence waver for the first time.
He swallowed hard, his breath catching as he whispered.
"This is bad..."

chapters.title: Chapter 921: Spell
chapters.content:
Chapter 921: Spell
"ROOOOOOOAAARRRR!!!"
The Monster King let out another earth-shaking roar, its claws tearing into the ground as it began its charge.
Its first attack was a wave of black energy, arcing toward Rey like a tidal wave of death.
~WHUUSH!~
Rey's instincts screamed, and he activated [Space-Shift], blinking several feet to the side just in time to avoid being engulfed. The ground where he had stood moments ago sizzled and blackened, proof of the attack's lethality.
"That would've hurt," he muttered, his heart pounding.
"The King wasn't done.
With shocking speed for its size, it lunged, its claws raking down toward him.
Rey pushed his [Physical Enhancement] to its limit, propelling himself backward and landing in a crouch. He rolled to the side as the beast slammed its massive fist into the ground, the impact sending tremors through the earth.
~BOOOOOM!~
Rey retaliated with a surge of electricity, launching an Electrical Surge toward the King. ~TZZZTTTZ!~
The lightning struck its thick scales but barely fazed the creature.
"GRRRRR..." It let out a threatening snarl, seemingly more annoyed than hurt, and opened its maw to unleash another wave of energy.
"Damn it," Rey hissed, dodging again with [Space-Shift], but the effort was starting to take its toll.
"Haa..."
His breathing was labored, and his muscles burned with fatigue.
His body bore the marks of the battle-deep cuts, bruises, and the sticky warmth of blood seeping through his torn clothes.
'It's unfortunate, but I don't have any Healing Skills.'
Level Ups didn't provide that, unfortunately.
The King was relentless, each attack growing more ferocious as if it were feeding off the fight. Rey clenched his fists, frustration building as he realized none of his current skills could deal a decisive blow.
Then he remembered.
"Status Information." A smirk played on his bloodied lips as he summoned his Status Window.
[STATUS WINDOW]
- Name: Rey Skylar
- Race: Human
- Class: NIL
- Level: 25 (12.90% EXP)
- Life Force: 5/15
- Mana Level: 21/25
- Combat Ability: 10/15
- Stat Points: 25
- Skills (Exclusive): [Doppel]
- Skills (Non-Exclusive): NIL
- Alignment: Chaotic Neutral
[Additional Information]
Unknown... no information has been provided.
[End Of Information]
His eyes scanned the screen, taking note of the 25 unspent Status Points he had amassed during his battles. Without hesitation, he allocated all of them to Mana, feeling an immediate surge of energy course through his body.
"It's time for a little experiment," he muttered, his smirk widening.
Whatever happened now depended on luck, but it was supposed to work in theory-at least, that was what he hoped for.
Rey reached deep into his memory, recalling a Spell he had learned on H'Trae.
It was a destructive technique for sure, but not a big deal for him at his peak. Still, considering his current situation, he knew it would be more than enough to solve this problem... if it was successful.
'Please work!'
He began the incantation, his hands moving in intricate patterns as a ball of fire began to form in front of him.
The King seemed to sense the danger and charged at him, its eyes glowing with fury.
Rey stood his ground, sweat beading on his forehead as he focused every ounce of his Mana
into the Spell.
"Grand Fireball!"
The words left his lips, and the fireball erupted forward-a massive, searing orb of destruction that illuminated the battlefield in brilliant red and orange. T
~VWUUUUUM!~
The heat was intense, scorching the air around it as it streaked toward the King.
The creature tried to evade, but it was too large, too slow. The fireball struck its chest with a deafening explosion, engulfing it in flames.
~BOOOOOOOOOM!~
The force of the blast sent a shockwave rippling through the area, knocking over smaller Monsters and sending debris flying.
When the fire dissipated, nothing remained of the King but a charred crater.
"It worked... it actually worked!"
Rey stood there, panting heavily, as the glowing words [You Have Leveled Up] appeared in
front of him.
A grin spread across his face despite his exhaustion.
'I partly didn't expect it to work because I'm on Earth and I wasn't sure if the theory of Magic applied here as it does for H'Trae, but apparently it does.'
This changed things for him entirely/
The remaining Monsters trembled at the sight, their confidence shattered.
Even the team watching from the ridge was speechless, their expressions a mixture of awe
and disbelief.
Rey wasn't done.
His blood was pumping, and he wasn't about to leave a single one of these creatures alive.
"You're next," he said, his voice low and menacing.
He activated [Camouflage], disappearing from sight, and reappeared behind a group of Monsters with [Space-Shift], striking them down with enhanced strength.
Another group tried to flee, but Rey's [Soundwave] disoriented them, leaving them vulnerable to a stream of water from [Moist Meter], which he froze mid-air to impale them.
Some Monsters attempted to scatter in different directions, but Rey's [High Sense] allowed him to track their movements. He leapt from one target to another, his shadow binding a group as he dispatched them with electrified punches.
The last Monster let out a desperate screech and sprinted toward the edge of the battlefield.
Rey extended his shadow to trip it, closing the gap with a swift [Space-Shift] and finishing it off with a crushing stone-enhanced blow.
Thanks to his increased Stats, he was much faster and stronger, so unlike his first experience with these creatures he was far more competent-able to beat them with one or two blows if
he really tried.
"Whew!"
When it was over, Rey stood amidst the corpses of dozens of Monsters, his chest heaving and his body drenched in blood and sweat. He looked up at his team on the ridge, who still hadn't moved, their shock evident even from this distance.
"Hehe... they must be quite surprised."
He wondered what to tell them this time as an excuse for the Fireball.
'I could tell them that it's a Special Ability I copied, and I just recovered some of my memories, which explains why I'm able to use it now.' He smiled. 'But how do I explain my
raised Stats?'
He could also attribute that to another Special Ability that allowed him to get stronger the
more he fought.
'Honestly, it doesn't matter what excuse I give at this point.' Rey thought to himself as he saw
the look in their eyes.
'They have to believe me... because I'm that strong.'

chapters.title: Chapter 922: Benefit Of Strength
chapters.content:
Chapter 922: Benefit Of Strength
"Haaa..."
Rey stood amidst the wreckage of the battlefield, his chest heaving as he caught his breath.
The acrid scent of burnt flesh still hung in the air, and the ground was littered with the remains of the Monsters he had singlehandedly defeated. His fingers twitched slightly as he opened his Status Window, eager to see the results of his efforts.
[STATUS WINDOW]
- Name: Rey Skylar
- Race: Human
- Class: NIL
- Level: 35 (2.13% EXP)
- Life Force: 15
- Mana Level: 50
- Combat Ability: 20
- Stat Points: 10
- Skills (Exclusive): [Doppel]
- Skills (Non-Exclusive): [Grand Magic Application]. [Grand Magic Mastery].
- Alignment: Chaotic Neutral
[Additional Information]
Unknown... no information has been provided.
[End Of Information]
His lips curved into a satisfied smirk as he took in the sight of his increased Level.
Reaching Level 35 was an impressive feat, but his eyes lingered on the EXP percentage, now crawling upward at a much slower rate.
"The higher I go, the harder it gets," Rey muttered to himself, his voice tinged with both frustration and determination.
"Stronger foes, huh? Guess I'll just have to hunt bigger fish."
That wasn't the only thing that went through his mind, however. One good look at his Status Window showed that he had acquired two Exclusive Skills-Skills that belonged to a certain Grand Mage of H'Trae.
'By activating that Fireball the way I did, I must have made the System believe that I had the Skill... or could it be that I fulfilled the requirements to have that skill, which is why the System added it in for me?' He wondered.
Regardless, it seemed to Rey that there was more than one way to get stronger.
'If I apply some of the things I already knew in H'Trae, it should be possible for me to regain some of my old Skills-at least at the basic level.'
That was good enough for a start.
'And now... for my [Doppel] collection.'
A quick check of his Doppel Skill list revealed a few new additions-abilities copied from the Monsters he'd just defeated.
One caught his attention: [Shadow Maelstrom], a Skill that created a vortex of shadow energy, drawing enemies toward its center before unleashing a crushing impact.
'That's what the Monster King used that time, huh? Cool!'
He couldn't help but feel optimistic.
"If I keep this up, I might just make it back to where I was before... though it's going to take some time."
He glanced up as the sound of hurried footsteps broke his thoughts.
Tess was the first to reach him, her face a mixture of astonishment and concern. The rest of the team followed close behind, their expressions mirroring hers.
"Rey!" Tess exclaimed, her voice almost shrill. "Are you okay? What the hell was that back there? You-You wiped out that King like it was nothing!"
The others chimed in, their voices overlapping in a chaotic combination of shock and curiosity.
"Was that fireball some kind of Ultimate Skill?"
"Where did you even learn to fight like that?"
"Are you seriously human?"
Rey raised his hands defensively, a tired laugh escaping his lips. "Whoa, one question at a time! I'm still catching my breath here."
Their bombardment of questions eased slightly, and Rey took the opportunity to craft a carefully edited version of the truth.
"It's not as crazy as it looks," he said with a sheepish grin. "I've been recovering bits and pieces of my memories lately. Turns out I used to have this Special Ability that helps me adapt to enemies I fight. The fireball? Just something I figured out I could do after observing that King's energy attacks."
Tess crossed her arms, her eyes narrowing slightly. "So, you're saying all of this sudden power is because of some dormant memory recovery?"
"Pretty much," Rey replied, shrugging. "I'm just as surprised as you are."
It wasn't a complete lie, but it wasn't the full truth either. Still, it seemed to satisfy the team for now.
"Well, whatever the reason, you're a beast," Josh admitted grudgingly, rubbing the back of his neck. "That fireball was insane, man. And the way you took down all those sentinels?
Respect."
Rey chuckled softly. "Thanks. Guess I got lucky."
Tess shook her head.
"Luck had nothing to do with it. But right now, we've got something important to do."
Rey raised an eyebrow. "Important?"
"Monster Cores," Tess said, pointing at the scattered remains of the defeated creatures.
"Especially from the Boss Monster. Those Cores are valuable-like, insanely valuable. The sentinels' Cores are worth a lot too, and even the Scouts' Cores back there have some value, though not as much."
Rey blinked in surprise. "Monster Cores? You mean those things inside their chests?"
Tess nodded. "Exactly. They're a power source, and they're used for all kinds of things- fueling weapons, enhancing equipment, even research. A Core from a King Monster like that? It could fetch a fortune... and besides, HQ needs as many resources as possible." Rey glanced at the Monster King's charred remains and the sentinels littering the area. He'd never considered the value of Monster Cores on Earth.
On H'Trae, such resources were rare and guarded fiercely.
"This world isn't so different after all," he murmured to himself, smiling faintly.
"You should rest up," Tess added. "You've done more than enough. We'll handle the
harvesting."
Rey started to protest. "I can help-"
"No," Tess interrupted firmly. "Sit. Rest. You've been through hell, and you've earned a
break."
Rey relented, settling onto a nearby rock and watching as the team began their work. They moved methodically, extracting the Cores with practiced precision.
As he observed, a wave of understanding washed over him. The hierarchy of strength and the rewards that came with it were universal. No matter the world, the strong were respected, admired, and treated differently.
A small smile tugged at the corners of his lips. "Being strong makes life a lot easier."
He leaned back, letting himself relax for the first time in what felt like hours. This world
might have its challenges, but with his strength growing steadily, Rey felt confident that he could carve out his place in it.
As the team continued to harvest the Cores, Rey's gaze drifted toward the horizon, where the
faint glow of dawn was beginning to break.
A new day was coming, and with it, new opportunities to rise even higher.

chapters.title: Chapter 923: The Rendezvous
chapters.content:
Chapter 923: The Rendezvous
[Later That Day]
Back at the base, the atmosphere was calmer but still buzzing with the energy of their recent success. Rey leaned against the rough wall of the meeting room, arms crossed, as Tess
addressed the team.
"Headquarters has finally reached out," She announced, her tone serious but laced with relief.
"We've received the coordinates for a rendezvous location."
The team listened intently, their expressions a mix of curiosity and concern.
Tess continued, "Josh and I will be going there to hand over the resources we've collected, exchange information, and receive our next directive."
Rey tilted his head slightly, curiosity piqued. "Directives?"
Tess nodded. "HQ gives us specific tasks regarding the Dragon King and his forces. These can range from sabotaging their supply lines to infiltrating strongholds or even launching direct assaults on any of their bases. They dictate the overall strategy, and we execute."
She paused, glancing briefly at Rey.
"Our last task was to investigate this area because of the strange energy wavelengths we detected. That's how we found you."
"Lucky timing," Rey said with a faint smirk.
Josh snorted. "For you, maybe. For us? That was a hell of a welcome gift."
Ignoring Josh's comment, Tess pressed on.
"We're supposed to deliver the resources we've gathered so far-Monster Cores, data, anything of value. In return, the representative will provide us with our next steps."
Rey nodded slowly, the gears in his mind turning.
It sounded like a tight, well-organized system-something he hadn't expected from a ragtag group of resistance fighters.
"Makes sense," he said after a moment. "But if this is such an important meeting, shouldn't you have more people going?"
Tess hesitated, her gaze flickering toward him. "We're keeping the team here to guard the base. Too many people would attract attention, and we can't risk compromising our location. Josh and I can handle it."
Rey straightened, his expression unreadable. "Then I'll come with you."
The room fell silent for a moment. Tess's brows furrowed.
"Rey, it's not that simple-"
"I can handle myself," Rey interrupted calmly. "You've seen what I'm capable of. If something happens out there, wouldn't it be better to have someone like me watching your back?"
Josh looked between Rey and Tess, his expression torn. "He's got a point, Tess. If things go south, he's a hell of a trump card to have."
Tess crossed her arms, clearly weighing her options.
Finally, she sighed. "Fine. But you follow orders, no questions asked. Got it?"
Rey nodded, a small smile tugging at his lips.
"Got it."
As the rest of the team voiced their support, Rey noted the shift in their attitudes. I
f it had been a few days ago, they would have flat-out refused, leaving him with no choice but
to accept it. But now, after proving himself as the strongest among them, they had no choice but to accommodate him.
"The strong are always indulged," he thought to himself, a hint of satisfaction in the thought.
"Prepare your gear," Tess said, her voice cutting through his musings. "We leave at dawn." Rey returned to his room and smiled.
The solitude of his small but private space allowed him to experiment with a few things, and by the end of things, he had two new Non-Exclusive Skills in his Status Window.
'This is good... very good.'
Just like this, he would steadily climb to his previous stature.
***********
The next morning arrived quickly, the rising sun casting a soft glow over the barren landscape. Rey stood outside the base, adjusting his equipment as Tess and Josh loaded supplies into a concealed vehicle.
'I didn't even notice they had vehicles hidden until today...' Rey thought to himself.
He wondered what else they were keeping from him, though he knew it was only a matter of time before he was fully integrated in their affairs.
At this point, he had already proven to them-without the shadow of a doubt.
'They need me more than I need them.'
"You ready?"
Tess asked, glancing over at him.
"Always," Rey replied with a smirk, sliding into the vehicle's back seat.
The drive was uneventful at first, the vehicle humming softly as it glided over the uneven terrain. Rey stared out the window, his mind wandering to the rendezvous ahead.
"What kind of person are we meeting?" he asked, breaking the silence.
Tess, seated in the passenger seat, glanced back at him. "HQ doesn't usually give specifics. Could be a senior officer, a courier, or even someone from the science division. Depends on what they need from us."
Josh, who was driving, added, "It's not just about who's there. It's about the information they bring. HQ doesn't mess around when it comes to strategy."
Rey nodded thoughtfully, his gaze returning to the horizon. "And who's running HQ? I mean, this Resistance seems a lot more organized than I expected."
Tess hesitated, as if debating how much to reveal. "No one knows for sure. There are rumors, of course—about a council, or maybe even a single leader pulling the strings. But whoever they are, they've managed to keep us united against the Dragon King."
Rey leaned back in his seat, mulling over her words.
A hidden leader orchestrating a resistance against a tyrant. It was almost poetic, in a way. "And the Dragon King," he said quietly. "What's the plan there? You think HQ actually has a shot at taking him down?"
Josh laughed bitterly. "That's the million-dollar question, isn't it?"
Tess's expression hardened. "We don't have the luxury of doubt. Every mission we complete, every resource we gather-it all adds up. One day, we'll be ready to face him. Until then, we
follow HQ's lead."
Rey didn't reply, his thoughts turning inward.
The Dragon King was a force to be reckoned with, but so was Rey.
He clenched his fists, a quiet resolve settling over him.
For now, he'd follow their lead. But when the time came, he knew he'd have to carve his own
path. The vehicle rumbled on, the rendezvous point drawing closer with each passing mile.
Whatever awaited them there, Rey was ready to face it.

chapters.title: Chapter 924: Family Surprise
chapters.content:
Chapter 924: Family Surprise
"We're here..."
The rendezvous spot was a secluded clearing, surrounded by dense trees that seemed to form a natural barrier.
The vehicle came to a halt, its engine humming softly before falling silent.
Rey stepped out, his eyes scanning the area.
The air was tense, thick with the weight of expectation and a slight hint of dread.
"Stay alert," Tess muttered as she adjusted the strap of her rifle. Josh nodded, his usual casual demeanor replaced by a sharp focus.
Rey's gaze shifted toward the edge of the clearing, where movement caught his eye.
Two figures emerged from the shadows-a man and a woman. The man walked confidently, his posture straight, exuding authority.
The woman followed a step behind, her eyes cold and calculating.
The moment Rey saw the man's face, his heart skipped a beat. He froze, his breath catching in his throat.
It was him.
"Rey?" the man's voice cut through the silence, laced with surprise. "What the hell...?"
Rey didn't answer immediately, his jaw tightening.
His older brother, Ezra, stood before him, looking almost exactly as he remembered-sharp features, piercing eyes, and that same smug expression that always seemed to say he was better than everyone else.
Ezra stepped closer, his gaze narrowing.
"Where have you been all this time? After the world went to hell, we thought you were dead. Mom and Dad didn't even bother to look for you. Can't say I blamed them."
Rey's fists clenched, but he remained silent.
'Here it comes... not even a minute since we reunited and he's already started...'
First, he circled around Rey, his eyes ogling every part of his body as he made his observations --but silent and loud-as he finally stood in front of him.
"Average as always..."
His remarks were loud and curt, and he even chuckled for extra effect.
"Mum and dad were right to have moved on so quickly. They shouldn't have cared as much as they did."
Rey remained quiet as he watched.
"And honestly?" Ezra continued, shrugging. "I didn't care either. You were always so... average. Nothing special. Just a dead weight. If you'd died, it wouldn't have made a difference to anyone."
Josh bristled, taking a step forward. "Hey! That's enough-"
"Stand down," Ezra snapped, his voice sharp. "This is a family matter. I'll speak to my brother without interruptions."
Tess shot Rey a concerned look, but Rey held up a hand, signaling her to stay out of it.
His older brother was definitely their superior, so they couldn't properly defend him even if they wanted to. Just based on their reaction, it was clear they wanted to say something to him, but hierarchy prevented them.
'Well... I can't say I blame them.' Rey leaked out a small smile. 'He's probably stronger than they are.'
It was at this point that he really wished he had an Appraisal Skill.
'But, oh well...'
Ezra smirked, taking Rey's silence as submission. "I'm honestly surprised you're still alive. The apocalypse doesn't exactly favor the weak. What, did you find some lucky group to leech off of? Or maybe you just hid while everyone else fought to survive?"
Rey finally looked up, his eyes locking with Ezra's. His expression was calm, almost serene, but his gaze was cold-so cold that Ezra faltered for a moment, the smugness wavering.
"You haven't changed a bit, Ezra," Rey said, his voice quiet but firm. "Still the same arrogant, self-absorbed prick you've always been. And you know what? I'm not surprised. Not in the least."
Ezra blinked, caught off guard by Rey's tone.
"But here's the thing," Rey continued, stepping forward. Each step seemed to radiate an unshakable confidence, the kind that made Ezra unconsciously take a step back. "
I'm not the person you remember. That weak, quiet little brother who let you walk all over him? He's gone."
Ezra's eyes widened slightly as Rey stopped just a few feet away.
For the first time, he seemed to notice the shift in Rey-the way he carried himself, the strength in his stance, the fire in his eyes.
Rey smiled coldly, a smile that didn't reach his eyes. "So, let me make this clear. From now on, you don't get to disrespect me. Not me, and not my team leader. The next time you try, I won't let it slide. Not even once."
Ezra shivered involuntarily, a chill running down his spine.
He tried to mask it with a sneer, but the confidence he usually wielded so effortlessly was
gone.
Without another word, Rey turned away.
"Tess," he called over his shoulder, his tone light again. "I'll patrol the perimeter. Signal me when you're done with the exchange."
Tess nodded, her expression a mix of pride and concern. "Got it."
As Rey walked off, Ezra stood frozen in place, his fists clenched at his sides. He watched his younger brother disappear into the trees, his mind racing.
This wasn't the Rey he remembered.
Not at all.
**************
The forest was quiet, save for the occasional rustle of leaves. Rey moved with purpose, his thoughts swirling but his heart steady.
Ezra's words, the scorn in his voice, the dismissal-none of it mattered. Not anymore.
"The person he remembers is gone," Rey thought, a small smile tugging at his lips. "Let him cling to his memories. I've moved on."
The world had changed, and so had Rey. And as he patrolled the area, his resolve only grew stronger. Whatever lay ahead, he would face it-not as the boy he once was, but as the man he
had become.
'What matters now is getting stronger. People like Ezra are simply mere distraction... a waste
of time and energy.'
[STATUS WINDOW]
- Name: Rey Skylar
- Race: Human
- Class: NIL
- Level: 35 (12.90% EXP)
- Life Force: 15
- Mana Level: 50
- Combat Ability: 20
- Stat Points: 10
- Skills (Exclusive): [Doppel]
- Skills (Non-Exclusive): [Grand Magic Application]. [Grand Magic Mastery]. [Grand Combat
Application]. [Grand Weapon Mastery]. [Grand Battle Aura]. [Grand Mana Regeneration].
- Alignment: Chaotic Neutral
[Additional Information]
Unknown... no information has been provided.
[End Of Information]

chapters.title: Chapter 925: Unexpected Mission
chapters.content:
Chapter 925: Unexpected Mission
||
Tension oozed in the air.
The clearing was quiet after Rey had departed, leaving Tess and Josh to handle the exchange with Ezra. Tess adjusted the strap of her weapon, her expression neutral as she faced the man who was both a superior and a thorn in her side.
Ezra leaned casually against a nearby tree, his arms crossed as he regarded her.
The woman accompanying him stood a step behind, her gaze cold and professional, though her hands deftly worked to log the resources Tess and Josh were handing over.
"So," Ezra began, his tone dripping with feigned curiosity, "how exactly did you find my dear brother?"
Tess met his gaze evenly.
"We discovered him in the aftermath of a wreckage not far from our base," she replied. "He was unconscious and injured, but somehow alive. We brought him back and patched him up. Since then, he's been helping out and pulling his weight."
Ezra raised an eyebrow. "Memory loss, you said?"
"Yes," Tess confirmed. "He doesn't remember how he ended up there or what happened before the wreckage. We're still piecing things together."
Ezra smirked, the expression more mocking than amused.
In his mind, he scoffed. 'Memory loss, huh? Convenient excuse. Typical Rey-always looking for a way to cover up his weaknesses. Let me guess, he's pretending to be some newfound paragon of strength now? Acting all confident to make himself seem less pathetic?'
He chuckled softly to himself, shaking his head.
'He can play his little charade for now, but the next time he steps out of line... I'll remind him of his place. No one challenges me and gets away with it.'
Turning his attention back to Tess, Ezra's smirk widened.
"You'd better keep your subordinate in check," he said, his tone suddenly sharp. "Rey might think he's grown a backbone, but it's your responsibility to make sure he doesn't embarrass himself-or you-again."
Tess's jaw tightened, but she forced a polite smile. "Understood, sir."
Josh, standing nearby, clenched his fists, his anger barely concealed. His knuckles whitened as he kept his gaze fixed on the ground, biting his tongue to keep from snapping at Ezra.
Ezra seemed pleased with himself, ignoring the obvious tension.
He gestured to his assistant, who stepped forward to gather the final inventory of resources Tess and Josh had brought.
"Now," Ezra said, his tone all business, "let's talk about your new mission."
Tess straightened, nodding attentively.
Ezra pulled out a tablet and tapped a few commands before handing it over to Tess.
The screen displayed maps and detailed notes.
"Your task is to investigate this location," he explained, pointing to a marked spot on the map. "It's a newly discovered stronghold of the Dragon King. HQ needs intel-layout, defenses, any troop movement patterns. You're to observe and report back. Absolutely no engagement. This is a reconnaissance mission, and it's sensitive."
Tess studied the tablet, nodding.
"Understood. We'll gather all the information and relay it to HQ."
Josh chimed in with a terse, "Got it."
Ezra glanced at both of them, seemingly satisfied.
"Good. Don't screw this up. HQ is counting on this data." He turned to his assistant, who was now efficiently packing the collected resources. "We'll be taking these back to HQ. My assistant will handle the inventory."
Without further pleasantries, Ezra waved them off and began walking toward his transport. His assistant followed, her hands full of the carefully packaged haul.
As the sound of Ezra's departure faded, Tess let out a long breath, her shoulders relaxing slightly.
Josh muttered a curse under his breath, shaking his head in frustration.
"Unbelievable," he grumbled. "That guy is insufferable. I don't know how you kept your
cool."
Tess gave him a wry smile.
"Practice." She handed the tablet to Josh. "Here, familiarize yourself with the mission details. I'll fill Rey in when we get back to the vehicle."
*********
Rey was leaning casually against the vehicle when Tess and Josh returned. He looked up as they approached, his usual calm smile in place.
"How did it go?" he asked, pushing off the side of the vehicle to meet them.
Tess sighed, rubbing her temple. "We've got a new mission."
Rey's eyes lit up, and he nodded. "Good news, then. That sounds manageable."
Josh snorted, his frustration still simmering. "Yeah, if we don't have to deal with him again anytime soon."
Rey chuckled softly, his gaze flicking toward Tess. "Sounds like it was eventful."
"You could say that," Tess replied, her tone dry.
She gestured toward the vehicle. "Let's get back to the base. We'll debrief everyone and start planning for the mission."
As they loaded into the vehicle and began the drive back, Rey leaned back in his seat, gazing out the window.
His mind wandered, not to Ezra's words, but to the mission ahead.
'Whatever it takes,' he thought, determination hardening his resolve. 'I'll inevitably prove that I'm not the person he thinks I am. Regardless, I'm not doing this for him, or for anyone
else.'
It was all selfish ambition.
'I've come too far to let anyone hold me back now.'
***********
[Moments Later]
Back at the base, the team gathered in the central hall where Tess had spread out a map of the region on the table. The room was dimly lit, the faint hum of the base's generators filling the silence as everyone leaned in to listen.
Tess stood at the head of the table, pointing to a marked location on the map.
"This is where we're headed next," she began. "HQ has identified it as a new stronghold for the Dragon King's forces. Our mission is reconnaissance-observe the area, gather intel on their defenses and troop movements, and report back. Absolutely no engagement unless it's
to defend yourselves."
Rey, standing near the back of the group with his arms crossed, frowned subtly at the words.
'No engagement?' he thought. 'Just spying on the enemy?'
This was bad... really bad.
'I can't accept this... it's not what I expected at all!'

chapters.title: Chapter 926: Mission Begins
chapters.content:
Chapter 926: Mission Begins
"The stronghold is well-fortified, and HQ believes it may serve as a supply hub. That means it's critical to gather as much information as possible without tipping them off to our presence. Stealth and precision are the keys to success."
Tess continued, unaware of Rey's inner turmoil.
Josh nodded seriously, and the rest of the team murmured their agreement.
But Rey's frown deepened.
'Stealth and precision are fine,' he thought, 'but they're not going to make me stronger.'
Tess glanced at him, her gaze briefly lingering on his unreadable expression, but she didn't call attention to it. She continued outlining the specifics of their route, the expected challenges, and the contingency plans.
It was a well-thought out and laid out plan, showing the competence of The Resistance HQ.
But... it was problematic-especially for Rey.
'This isn't good.'
***************
As the meeting wrapped up and the team began to disperse, Rey stayed behind, his mind racing.
He wasn't upset with Tess or the mission itself-he understood the importance of reconnaissance.
But it didn't sit well with him.
'I didn't come back to this world to tiptoe around.'
He couldn't afford to.
He clenched his fists, his frustration bubbling beneath the surface.
The battle at the wreckage, the monsters he'd defeated, and the sense of power he'd felt coursing through him-it had lit a fire within him that wasn't so easily extinguished.
"Rey?"
He looked up to see Tess standing a few steps away, watching him carefully. The rest of the team had left, leaving them alone in the room.
"You looked... dissatisfied," she said cautiously.
Rey forced a small smile. "It's nothing. Just thinking."
Tess raised an eyebrow, clearly unconvinced. "About?"
He hesitated, then sighed.
"I get why HQ wants intel. It's important. But..." He trailed off, searching for the right words. "I need to fight. I need to push myself harder, face stronger opponents. Spying on the enemy won't help me get stronger."
Tess studied him for a moment, her expression unreadable.
Then she crossed her arms. "Rey, I understand where you're coming from. But this isn't just about getting stronger. It's about survival. If we rush in without knowing what we're up against, we'll all die."
"I know," he admitted, his voice quieter. "But I can't shake the feeling that I'm wasting time."
"Wasting time?" Tess tilted her head. "Rey, you've already proven yourself. You don't have to rush this. Strength isn't just about fighting-it's about strategy, about knowing when to act and when to wait. Believe me, I've learned that the hard way."
Her words struck a chord, but the restless fire within him didn't waver.
He gave her a faint nod, more out of politeness than agreement.
"Just... trust the process," Tess added, placing a hand on his shoulder. "We'll get through this, and there will be plenty of fights ahead. For now, let's focus on the mission."
Rey nodded again, this time with more sincerity. "I'll try."
Tess smiled and squeezed his shoulder lightly before turning to leave.
As she walked away, Rey's thoughts continued to churn.
'Trust the process? Maybe. But I can't let myself stagnate.'
After experiencing what war was like in H'Trae, and exactly how cruel the Dragon Emperor's forces could be, it wasn't something any of the humans on Earth could afford either.
He glanced back at the map on the table, the marked stronghold seeming to taunt him.
He'd follow Tess's lead for now, but deep down, he knew he'd have to find his own way to grow stronger-whether that meant stepping outside the mission's boundaries or seeking challenges elsewhere.
For now, he'd bide his time.
But the fire within him was far from extinguished.
*********
[The Next Day]
The base felt quieter than usual after the team left.
Rey stood in the common area, watching the vehicle disappear over the horizon through a narrow window. Tess hadn't even given him a chance to suggest joining the mission-her decision had been firm, leaving him behind with only a brief explanation that the mission required discretion and caution.
He hadn't argued.
He understood the reasoning behind her decision. His restlessness during the last discussion had been obvious, and Tess likely feared that his impatience might jeopardize the operation.
Still, the sting of being excluded gnawed at him.
'She's probably right, at least when it involves the mission from HQ...' he thought. 'But that doesn't mean I have to sit around doing nothing.'
Rey turned back to the few team members who had stayed behind.
"I'll be training in my room," he announced, his tone even. "Don't disturb me."
They nodded without question, accustomed to his growing need for isolation when he
trained.
Once in his room, Rey locked the door and leaned against it, closing his eyes.
He murmured a chant under his breath, weaving a concealment Spell around himself. The faint shimmer of magic engulfed him, rendering him invisible to sight and detection.
With a flick of his wrist, he cast another spell, a soft glow of energy forming beneath his feet as he activated a Flight Spell. The window slid open noiselessly, and Rey slipped out into the evening sky, rising silently into the air.
His heart pounded with excitement and determination.
'Tess doesn't trust me to follow the mission's rules, so it's best I remove myself from the equation and act independently...'
He followed the team's vehicle from a safe distance, keeping his concealment spell active.
The journey took hours, the vehicle weaving through rough terrain before finally stopping near a cluster of jagged hills. From above, Rey observed as Tess, Andrew, and Dexter emerged, their silhouettes barely visible against the rocky backdrop.
Tess gathered the team and spoke in hushed tones, her hand pointing toward an opening in the ground that led to what appeared to be an underground structure.
Rey adjusted his position to get a better look.
The opening was small and partially hidden by debris, the entrance shrouded in darkness.
Tess divided the group.
She, Andrew, and Dexter would enter, relying on their unique abilities to stay hidden, while
the others kept watch outside.
Rey watched all of this with a smile, all preparations made on his own end.
'Looks like we're about to begin.'

chapters.title: Chapter 927: WithinnThe Cavern
chapters.content:
Chapter 927: WithinnThe Cavern
The plan seemed solid, and Rey could appreciate the logic of their approach.
'Dexter can turn invisible, and Andrew can manipulate his shadow in many ways, while Tess can teleport... all useful abilities for movement and stealth necessary for this mission.'
Everything was in place, and it was with that same logic that he was also making his move. He had all of their Skills and even more, so he would be fine.
'Also, I'll be able to help them out in case they need help... so this is fine too.' He thought, descending carefully to land near the entrance.
His concealment spell remained active as he approached the shadowed trio and they entered the welcoming maw of the dark cave.
Inside the underground structure, the air was cold and damp.
Tess led the way, her every movement deliberate and precise. Andrew melted into the shadows, his presence almost imperceptible, while Dexter shimmered faintly before vanishing entirely, his invisibility spell engaged.
Rey followed at a safe distance, his own concealment ensuring he wouldn't be detected.
The corridor sloped downward, dimly illuminated by faintly glowing moss that clung to the walls. Strange symbols were etched into the stone, their meanings unclear but their presence unsettling.
Tess raised a hand, signaling the group to stop. She crouched low, her sharp eyes scanning the area ahead.
Andrew and Dexter held their positions, waiting for her command.
"There's movement up ahead," she whispered, her voice barely audible. "Stay sharp."
Rey's heart quickened as he focused his gaze, spotting faint shapes moving in the distance. Creatures, humanoid but distorted, shuffled through the passage, their elongated limbs dragging along the ground.
Their low, guttural growls echoed faintly.
Tess motioned for the group to move forward carefully. Andrew's shadows extended, creeping along the walls and floor to obscure their presence. Dexter flickered into visibility for a brief moment before vanishing again, his invisibility spell struggling against the drain of prolonged use.
Rey followed with practiced silence, his curiosity piqued by the creatures.
He observed their movements closely, noting the way they seemed to patrol in a synchronized pattern.
'Guardians, maybe?' he speculated. 'This place must be important to the Dragon King's forces.'
The group reached a fork in the corridor.
Tess gestured for Andrew to scout the left path while she and Dexter continued down the right. Rey hesitated for a moment before deciding to follow Tess.
The corridor narrowed, forcing them to move single file. The glowing moss grew sparser, plunging the passage into near-total darkness.
Rey activated a minor Night Vision spell, his eyes adjusting to the dim light.
As they pressed on, the sound of grinding stone reached their ears. Tess raised a fist, signaling
a halt. Ahead, a massive stone door loomed, its surface covered in intricate carvings.
Two of the distorted creatures stood guard, their eerie eyes scanning the area.
"We'll observe for a moment," Tess whispered to Dexter. "Look for patterns in their movements."
Rey, standing a short distance behind them, frowned. The creatures were formidable, but nothing he couldn't handle.
His instincts urged him to act, to test his strength against these foes.
No, he told himself. Not yet. This is their mission, not mine.
He clenched his fists, forcing himself to stay hidden. For now, he'd watch and wait.
'For now...'
***********
The dim, narrow corridors seemed endless, twisting and turning like a labyrinth designed to swallow intruders whole. Tess led the way with precision, her senses heightened as she carefully navigated the path ahead.
Andrew's shadows crawled along the walls like living tendrils, ready to conceal the group at a moment's notice, while Dexter remained close, shimmering faintly as his invisibility spell wavered under strain.
Rey followed silently from the shadows, his spell keeping him out of sight and undetected. The deeper they went, the more oppressive the atmosphere became.
The faint luminescence of the moss on the walls gave way to total darkness, and an unnatural chill permeated the air.
Finally, the corridor widened into a massive cavern.
Rey stayed hidden at the upper edge of the space, hovering just below the ceiling with his Flight Spell. From his vantage point, he could see everything.
The cavern was unlike anything he had imagined.
Rows of cages filled with monstrous creatures lined the walls, their bars glowing faintly with a strange energy that kept the creatures restrained. The beasts varied in size and shape- some were hulking brutes with jagged claws and teeth, while others were smaller and more agile, their sharp eyes darting around as if searching for prey.
In the center of the cavern, a group of humans bustled around a set of makeshift laboratories.
The setup was crude but functional, with tables covered in vials, syringes, and glowing containers filled with unknown substances. Machines hummed softly, their blinking lights casting eerie shadows across the walls.
At the center of it all stood a man in a white lab coat, his sharp features illuminated by the glow of a nearby monitor. He held a clipboard in one hand and a syringe filled with a bright, pulsating liquid in the other.
"Another batch," he muttered to himself, his voice carrying across the cavern. "Let's see if this one can hold together for more than a few minutes."
He approached one of the cages, where a massive, lizard-like creature growled and thrashed against its restraints.
The scientist jabbed the syringe into the creature's neck and stepped back, watching intently as the liquid coursed through its veins.
The transformation was immediate.
"ROOOOOOAAAAARRRR!!!" The creature roared in agony, its muscles bulging and its body growing larger with every passing second.
Its eyes glowed an unnatural red, and its movements became more erratic.
For a moment, it seemed the experiment had succeeded.
But then, the creature's body convulsed violently, and its flesh began to tear apart as if unable
to contain its newfound power. With one final, agonizing roar, it collapsed in a heap, lifeless.
The scientist sighed and scribbled notes on his clipboard.
"Damnit..." He said, his tone a mixture of frustration and resignation.
"Another failure."

chapters.title: Chapter 928 - 928: Stealing Into The Night
chapters.content:
"We're close, but it's still not enough."
The words of the scientist echoed within the vast space.
His words were filled with tinges of annoyance, but the man remained calm.
Tess, Andrew, and Dexter had taken cover behind a stack of crates near the cavern's edge. Tess signaled for them to remain silent as they observed the scene. Dexter's invisibility flickered briefly, and he adjusted his position, inadvertently knocking over a small metal tool that clattered to the ground.
The sound echoed through the cavern like a gunshot.
"Who's there?" the scientist barked, spinning around. The guards flanking the lab drew their weapons and began scanning the area, their eyes narrowing as they searched for intruders.
Tess motioned urgently for her team to retreat.
Andrew's shadows engulfed them, and Dexter activated his invisibility again, though it sputtered weakly as the strain of prolonged use took its toll.
Rey, still concealed above, tensed as he watched the guards fan out.
One of them approached the stack of crates where Tess and her team had been hiding moments ago. He held his breath, ready to intervene if necessary. But Tess and her team moved with practiced skill, slipping away undetected and making their way back toward the exit.
The scientist frowned, his gaze lingering on the crates.
After a moment, he turned back to his work, muttering to himself.
"Probably just a rat. Back to it."
Rey exhaled quietly, relief washing over him as he followed Tess and her team from a safe distance.
The team reached the exit without further incident, emerging into the cool night air.
Tess let out a sigh of relief, her expression grim as she turned to her comrades.
"That was close," she said, her voice low. "Too close. We need to report this to HQ immediately."
Andrew nodded, his shadows dissipating as he relaxed his stance. Dexter collapsed to the ground, visibly drained.
"I'm sorry," he muttered. "I nearly got us caught."
Tess placed a reassuring hand on his shoulder. "You didn't. That's what matters. Let's regroup and debrief."
The team that kept watch gathered together with Tess' group, happy to see their comrades made it out safely, though surprise was written on their faces due to the fact that they didn't expect it to be so soon.
Rey watched from a distance, still concealed.
His mind raced with everything he had seen—the breeding, the experiments, the unstable transformations.
'So it really is true… humans are working for the Dragon Emperor, he thought, his fists clenching.
'Why?'
Tess had already given him some of the reasons—one of them being religious fanaticism and selfish obsession with higher authority.
Still, he wasn't inclined to understand the logic behind them.
'Maybe it's because I've seen just what that thing is capable of… I can say for sure.' Rey's eyes narrowed as the image of the Dragon Emperor flickered in his mind.
'That entity is pure evil.'
As Tess and her team prepared to return to the base, Rey remained in the shadows, his resolve hardening.
'I'll need to get to the bottom of this…' He told himself silently. 'One way or another.'
************
The return to the base was marked by a heavy silence, each member of the team absorbed in their thoughts. Tess called for an immediate meeting upon their arrival, summoning everyone to the common area.
Rey emerged from his room, stretching casually, as though he had spent the entire evening in quiet isolation.
If anyone suspected otherwise, they didn't show it.
Tess stood at the center of the group, her arms crossed as she began relaying the details of their findings. The dim lighting of the common area cast deep shadows across her face, highlighting the seriousness of the situation.
"They're breeding monsters," she began, her voice firm. "And I think they're trying to evolve them too… using some kind of chemical solution to force rapid growth. The process is unstable, but if they succeed in perfecting it..."
She didn't need to finish the sentence. Everyone understood the implications.
"What do we do now?" Rey asked, stepping forward.
His expression was calm, but his eyes betrayed the storm of thoughts swirling in his mind.
"We can't just sit here. If we destroy the facility, we could stop this madness before it escalates. We could interrogate the researcher, find out who's behind this operation, and put an end to it for good."
The room fell silent as everyone turned to Tess. She sighed, her shoulders slumping slightly.
"That's not how it works, Rey," she said, her tone patient but firm. "Our job is to observe and report. HQ will decide the next steps. We've already sent an encrypted message detailing our findings. They'll determine a rendezvous point where we can debrief."
Rey frowned but said nothing, the disappointment evident on his face.
Tess seemed to notice but pressed on. "I understand your frustration, Rey, but we have to follow protocol. Acting on our own could jeopardize the mission—and all of us."
"I get it," Rey replied, his voice measured. He forced a small smile and nodded. "You're right. We should wait for HQ's orders."
The meeting concluded shortly after, with everyone dispersing to their respective quarters.
Tess lingered for a moment, her gaze fixed on Rey as though she wanted to say something, but ultimately she left without a word.
***********
Rey lay on his bed, staring at the ceiling. The room was dark and quiet, but his mind refused to follow suit. Images of the underground facility flashed through his thoughts—the cages filled with writhing beasts, the scientist injecting his grotesque creations, the lifeless carcasses of failed experiments.
'We're just going to let this continue?' he thought, clenching his fists. 'What if HQ decides not to act in time?'
Rey knew full well the limits of a bureaucratic system and how often it failed when it truly counted.
He sat up abruptly, running a hand through his hair in frustration. Sleep was a distant possibility. His instincts screamed at him to do something, to act before it was too late.
Sliding out of bed, Rey moved to the window, staring out at the moonlit landscape. He could see the faint outlines of the wilderness beyond the base, dark and foreboding.
"I can't let this go," he muttered to himself, his voice barely above a whisper. "If no one else will act, I will."
Rey began to gather his gear, his movements deliberate and quiet.
He slipped on his boots, secured his weapons, and double-checked his spells. He wouldn't need much—just enough to get back to the facility and carry out his plan.
As he strapped on his belt, he paused for a moment, his reflection catching his eye in the small, cracked mirror by his bed. The man staring back at him was no longer the average, timid person he was when he first returned to Earth.
'Looks like my muscles have gotten a lot more pronounced… that's good.'
He had changed drastically in the past few days.
And he wasn't going to let anyone—not Tess, not HQ, and certainly not his brother—dictate his actions anymore.
'They've done their part… now it's my turn.'
With one last glance at the sleeping base, Rey activated his concealment spell and slipped into the night, the cold air biting at his skin.

chapters.title: Chapter 929 - 929: Rey's Assault
chapters.content:
The facility loomed ahead, an ominous structure hidden beneath the earth's surface.
Rey stood at the entrance, the faint glow of the moonlight casting long shadows across the jagged rocks surrounding the area. The air was thick with tension, and his pulse quickened in anticipation of the fight to come.
He placed a hand on the hilt of the sword he had summoned with Magic moments earlier, its blade shimmering faintly in the darkness.
Rey took a deep breath, steadying his thoughts.
He had no intention of sneaking in this time.
'Let's see how they handle a frontal assault,' he thought, a smirk forming on his lips.
Gathering his magic, he created a glowing orb of energy in his palm, its light illuminating his determined expression.
With a flick of his wrist, he hurled the orb at the facility's entrance.
~BOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMM!!!~
The explosion that followed was deafening, shaking the ground and sending debris flying.
Almost immediately, the air was filled with guttural growls and hisses as the facility's defenses came alive.
Rey's eyes narrowed as figures emerged from the shadows—monsters of various shapes and sizes, their eyes glowing with a feral light. They charged at him in unison, their movements coordinated and precise.
"Domesticated," Rey muttered, his tone laced with disdain. "Figures they'd train these creatures to guard their dirty little secrets."
These people were very smart about it too.
'This way anyone who sees this from afar and even suspects any activity inside will probably think it's a Monster Den and stay away.'
Rey also had a few other thoughts going on in his mind, but he couldn't afford to dwell on them.
The first wave of monsters lunged at him, but Rey was ready.
~VWUUSH!~
He activated [Battle Aura], a surge of crimson energy enveloping his body. The aura crackled with raw power, heightening his senses and sharpening his reflexes.
The monsters hesitated for a split second, sensing the danger, but it was too late. Rey dashed forward, his sword slicing through the air with unparalleled precision.
His [Grand Weapon Mastery] allowed him to wield the blade as though it were an extension of his arm.
Each swing was calculated, each movement deliberate.
A wolf-like beast leaped at him, but Rey sidestepped effortlessly, his sword cutting through its side in a single, fluid motion.
Another creature—a massive, bear-like monster with spiked fur—charged at him, its claws slashing through the air. Rey ducked under its swipe and retaliated with a powerful upward slash, the blade glowing faintly as it cleaved through the beast's thick hide.
~WHISH!~
The monsters came at him relentlessly, but Rey's [Grand Combat Application] allowed him to adapt to their every move.
A serpent-like creature lunged at him from the side, its fangs dripping with venom.
Rey spun on his heel, his blade arcing through the air to sever the serpent's head before it could strike.
~SWUSH!~
As the battle raged on, Rey's confidence grew.
He moved with a grace and power that felt almost instinctual, his body and mind working in perfect harmony.
It almost felt like he was in H'Trae again.
"Is this all you've got?" he called out, his voice cutting through the chaos. "I expected more from the people running this operation!"
His taunt seemed to trigger a response. From the shadows emerged a larger, more formidable monster—a hulking brute with armored plates covering its body and glowing red eyes that burned with rage.
Rey's smirk widened. "Now we're talking."
The brute roared and charged at him, its massive fists slamming into the ground with enough force to create a shockwave.
~BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!!!~
Rey leaped into the air, avoiding the impact, and brought his sword down in a powerful strike aimed at the creature's exposed neck. The blade glanced off the monster's armor with a sharp clang, and Rey landed gracefully, his mind already analyzing the situation.
Its armor is too tough for a direct attack. I'll need to find a weak spot.
The brute swung its massive arm at him, and Rey rolled out of the way, narrowly avoiding the blow.
He activated [Combat Sense], his mind flooding with information about the creature's movements and potential vulnerabilities.
The joints, he realized, his eyes locking onto the gaps in the creature's armor. That's where I'll strike.
The brute charged again, but this time, Rey was ready.
He ducked under its swing and delivered a precise slash to the back of its knee. The creature let out a pained roar, its movements faltering as it stumbled forward.
Rey didn't hesitate.
He surged forward, his blade cutting into the creature's other leg with ruthless efficiency.
"Guaaarrrk!"
The brute collapsed to its knees, its armored body crashing to the ground with a resounding thud.
With one final leap, Rey brought his sword down on the creature's neck, the blade piercing through the exposed flesh.
~SQUELCH!~
The brute let out a final, guttural roar before falling silent, its massive body going limp.
Rey stood over the fallen beast, his chest heaving as he caught his breath. His aura flickered for a moment before fading, the crimson energy dissipating into the night.
The remaining monsters hesitated, their instincts urging them to flee. Rey raised his sword, its blade gleaming ominously.
"Go ahead," he said, his voice low and menacing. "Run back to your masters. Let them know I'm coming."
The monsters scattered, disappearing into the shadows as Rey lowered his weapon. He glanced back at the facility, his expression hardening.
"This is just the beginning," he muttered, stepping toward the entrance once more.
'Hopefully this is enough to let the people inside know that I mean business… so I should be expecting even more opponents for round two.'
He could do this the entire night, but he most likely wouldn't have to.
'As long as I'm able to Level Up and stop whatever is going on here… I'll consider tonight a big win for me.'
Most importantly, he would leave no trace of his usual fighting style.
'It's why I'm choosing to use Martial Arts rather than my standard Magic or Skills.'
Either way, those thoughts were only secondary.
'What matters now isn't Tess and the rest of her team… but whatever comes out of that cave next.'

chapters.title: Chapter 930 - 930: Pushback
chapters.content:
"It's about time…"
Rey leaned against the jagged rocks near the entrance, his sword resting casually on his shoulder.
The air had grown eerily silent after the last of the monsters fled.
He expected something more than just beasts guarding this place, and soon enough, his patience paid off. From the shadows emerged five figures, all clad in uniformed attire.
Their matching dark gray gear bore insignias Rey didn't recognize, but the way they moved—calculated and confident—told him they weren't amateurs.
'Are they the organized security units that the scientists of this place employed to do their bidding?'
That had two possible implications.
'They could either be simple mercenaries, or they could also be directly tied to the Dragon Emperor and serve him like fanatics—perhaps something in the middle.'
If it was the former, then he wouldn't expect much information from them. Mercenaries hardly had the avenue to ask questions, and their main task would be to simply work for their money, so they were probably useless to him.
They probably weren't aware of the atrocities taking place in—
'No… I can't think like that.' Rey told himself. 'They're guilty by association, and that's what matters to me.'
"State your name and affiliation," the leader demanded, stepping forward.
He was a tall man with sharp features, and his piercing eyes scanned Rey with suspicion.
Rey tilted his head, his expression one of boredom.
"And if I don't feel like it?"
The leader's jaw tightened, but he kept his composure. "You've already caused enough trouble. By the time we're done with you, you'll tell us everything we want to know."
At this, Rey couldn't suppress a grin. He took a step forward, his sword now at his side, its tip grazing the ground.
"I think you've got things backward," he said, his voice low but dripping with confidence. "When I'm done with you, you'll be begging to tell me everything I want to know."
The leader sneered. "Big talk from someone who doesn't know who he's dealing with. Get him!"
