'Looks like they just gave me permission to do what I want with them…'
Rey's smile widened as soon as he recognized that the men had become fair game to him.
He wouldn't feel bad even if they ended up dead.
The clash began with the five of them charging at once, their movements synchronized like a well-rehearsed routine. Each one activated a distinct Special Ability, the air around them crackling with energy.
The first to reach Rey was a burly man whose arms began to morph into iron, creating massive fists that slammed toward Rey with earth-shattering force. Rey sidestepped the attack with ease, his enhanced reflexes allowing him to dance around the man's strikes.
"Too slow," Rey taunted, delivering a precise kick to the man's knee, forcing him to stagger backward.
The second enemy, a lithe woman with glowing blue tattoos, summoned tendrils of gooey liquid that shot toward Rey like whips. Rey spun his sword, slicing through the liquid constructs as he closed the distance between them.
"You'll have to try harder than that," he said, smirking as the woman's eyes widened in frustration.
Before he could strike, a sudden burst of wind knocked him off balance. Another enemy, a man with spiky hair and a smug grin, manipulated the air around him, creating powerful gusts that threatened to hurl Rey into the rocks.
Rey planted his feet firmly on the ground, activating [Battle Aura] to anchor himself. The crimson energy surged around him, counteracting the wind and allowing him to lunge forward.
The fourth attacker, a smaller man with glowing red eyes, unleashed a barrage of fireballs that filled the air with searing heat.
Rey dodged each one with incredible agility, weaving through the onslaught like a shadow.
"Annoying," Rey muttered, closing in on the man and landing a solid punch to his gut.
The final enemy, a woman with a staff, stood back, murmuring under her breath. A shimmering barrier formed around her teammates, and Rey could feel his attacks weakening as they struck the glowing field.
"A support specialist, huh?" Rey said, his eyes narrowing. "Guess I'll save you for last."
He shifted his focus back to the others, his movements becoming more fluid as he activated [Grand Combat Application].
His mind analyzed their patterns, predicting their next moves before they made them.
The metal-fisted man charged again, but Rey ducked under his swing and delivered an upward slash, the blade striking the gap between the man's armor plates.
"ARGHHHH!" The man roared in pain, stumbling backward.
The water manipulator tried to trap him with a sphere of water, but Rey shattered it with a burst of energy from his sword.
He darted toward her, his blade grazing her shoulder before she could retreat.
"Kyaaahh!"
The wind user attempted to create a vortex to trap him, but Rey dashed through it, his aura shielding him from the turbulent currents.
He reached the man in an instant, delivering a devastating blow to his side.
The fire user launched another volley of flames, but Rey countered with a swift strike, the force of his blade extinguishing the flames mid-air.
As the support specialist reinforced her barrier, Rey grinned.
He knew it was time to end this.
Raising his hand, he channeled the power of [Shadow Maelstrom], a Skill he had obtained from the Monster King he recently defeated. Dark energy began to swirl around him, forming a vortex of shadows that pulsed with ominous power.
The enemies hesitated, their confidence wavering as the oppressive force of the maelstrom grew.
"Get ready," Rey said, his voice calm but deadly. "Because I'm ending this now."
~VWUUUUUUSSSHHH!!!~
With a flick of his wrist, the maelstrom surged forward, engulfing the five enemies in a storm of darkness. They cried out in shock as the shadows tore through their defenses, shattering the barrier and leaving them dazed and disoriented.
When the maelstrom dissipated, the five of them were sprawled on the ground, groaning in pain. Rey stood over them, his sword resting on his shoulder once more.
"Now," he said, his smirk returning, "who wants to start talking?"

chapters.title: Chapter 931 - 931: Evolution
chapters.content:
"Now then… let's begin."
The five were bound tightly by a glowing web of energy, Rey's spell holding them in place as they squirmed and struggled.
They glared at him with a mixture of fury and fear, but none dared to speak. Rey stood before them, his sword resting lightly in his hand, his eyes cold and unrelenting.
"Let's make this simple," Rey began, his tone sharp and cutting. "Who are you, and what's the purpose of this operation?"
At first, they said nothing, but a faint shimmer of the binding spell sent jolts of pain through their bodies, making one of them cry out.
"Alright! Alright, we'll talk!"
The leader of the group, a man with stone-gray eyes and a trembling voice, spoke up. "We... we belong to the Cult of the Dragon Emperor. This base... it's part of his plan. Please, don't kill us!"
Rey's expression darkened, but he motioned for the man to continue. "And this research? What's it for?"
The man hesitated, glancing nervously at his comrades. Rey's sword flashed in the dim light, the tip grazing the man's neck.
"Don't make me ask twice."
"It's to strengthen monsters," the man blurted out, sweat dripping down his face. "We've been infusing them with the Emperor's essence, trying to make them more powerful. The Emperor believes this is the key to his victory—an unstoppable army of enhanced beasts under his control!"
Rey's stomach churned at the words.
"And what's in it for you?"
"E-excuse me?" The five looked a little confused as they heard the question.
"What is in it for you if you fulfil your Emperor's wish? You don't strike me as overly selfless."
"We—well… we were promised… a part of his new empire." One of them mumbled.
"Yeah… we will get our own territories and get to rise above everyone who used to look down on us in the new world."
"I just want to survive… honestly."
"We will get more power if we do this… and power is all that matters right now… no, even before the Dragon Emperor came. His presence only made us see the truth that we were blind to all this time."
"The Dragon Emperor is unstoppable anyway." The last one said. "If you can't beat em… join em!"
Hearing all their words caused Rey's brow to furrow in rage and disgust.
His grip on his sword tightened as his anger flared. "You've betrayed humanity for power? For dominion? You're no better than the monsters you're creating."
Before the cultists could respond, a deep, resonant voice echoed through the cavern, freezing everyone in place.
"You're correct, young man," the voice said, dripping with condescension. "They are traitors, and traitors deserve punishment."
The five cultists' faces contorted in sheer terror as they began to scream, begging for mercy.
Rey watched as their faces turned death pale in an instant.
Whatever had just sounded… it was a subject of immense horror to them.
"No! Please! Don't do this!"
"Please spare us… spare me!"
"We had no choice! We had to—"
But it was too late.
Their bodies convulsed violently as the same dark energy they had used to manipulate monsters surged through them.
Their forms twisted grotesquely, bones cracking and skin splitting as they transformed into monstrous versions of themselves, each one reflecting their elemental abilities.
The leader's body hardened into metal, his limbs bulging grotesquely as sharp spikes jutted from his back. The water manipulator turned into a serpentine creature with flowing, liquid-like skin. The fire user became a blazing, hulking beast with molten veins, and the wind manipulator's body stretched unnaturally, his limbs thinning into razor-sharp gusts. The support specialist morphed into an ethereal, ghostly figure surrounded by an impenetrable aura.
"Attack him," the voice commanded, its tone cold and unwavering.
The monsters lunged at Rey, their newfound power radiating with menace.
But Rey was already prepared.
~WUUUM!~
He activated a barrier spell, a dome of shimmering energy enveloping him just as the first attack struck. The stone beast's massive fists crashed against the barrier, sending ripples across its surface but leaving Rey unharmed.
"You were humans once," Rey said, his voice laced with both disgust and pity. "Now you're just mindless pawns."
With a flick of his hand, Rey channeled a devastating spell.
His magic surged through the air, gathering into a dense sphere above him.
"This ends now."
The sphere erupted into a storm of energy, cascading toward the five monsters.
~BOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMM!!!~
The blast consumed them entirely, their monstrous forms disintegrating into ash. When the dust settled, nothing remained but silence and the faint smell of ozone.
Rey lowered his hand, his expression hard.
"What a waste."
From the shadows, slow, deliberate clapping echoed through the cave. Rey turned to see a figure stepping forward, a man with a calm demeanor and sharp, calculating eyes. He wore a pristine white lab coat, stark against the dark surroundings.
"Impressive," the man said, his voice smooth and unhurried. "You're far more capable than I expected. Allow me to introduce myself—Dr. Shwartz."
Rey's eyes narrowed. "The scientist."
"Indeed," Dr. Shwartz replied, a faint smile playing on his lips. "And you must be the intruder who's been causing such a ruckus. I must admit, you've proven to be quite the distraction."
Rey leveled his sword at the man. "What's your goal here?"
Dr. Shwartz spread his arms, as if presenting himself. "Evolution, my dear boy. The world as it stands is stagnant, weak. The Dragon Emperor has shown us the way forward—a path to true strength, to perfection. These experiments are merely the first step."
"Perfection?" Rey scoffed. "You're turning people into monsters. That's not perfection—that's madness."
Dr. Shwartz's smile widened, his eyes gleaming with a twisted fervor. "Madness is merely a matter of perspective. In time, you'll see the beauty in what we're creating. But for now..."
He gestured toward the shadows, and a rumbling sound filled the cave. Rey instinctively shifted into a defensive stance, his grip tightening on his sword as something massive began to emerge from the depths.
"I'll leave you with a little demonstration of my work," Dr. Shwartz said, stepping back into the darkness.
"Consider it... a glimpse of what's to come."

chapters.title: Chapter 932 - 932: An Abomination
chapters.content:
"Fine by me. Let's see what your so-called evolution is made of."
Rey smirked, his adrenaline surging as he wanted to step forward to confront the epitome of insanity before him.
Then—
"GRRRRRRR…."
His eyes widened as a colossal beast lumbered into the light, its form a horrifying amalgamation of various monsters. Its eyes glowed with unnatural intensity, and its growl reverberated through the cavern.
'What the hell… is that?' Even Rey was shocked by what he was looking at.
The creature that emerged from the cave was gargantuan, its silhouette outlined by the faint glow of torches scattered around the cavern walls.
Its body was an unholy fusion of a dragon and a monstrous chimera—scales gleamed with a molten sheen, claws as sharp as blades tore at the ground with every step, and a pair of grotesque wings stretched wide, dripping with dark ichor.
Its eyes glowed an ominous crimson, filled with unrestrained fury and power.
Dr. Shwartz stood proudly behind the beast, his voice tinged with a mixture of excitement and mania.
"Beautiful, isn't it? The process remains unstable for most creatures, but this one—oh, this one is perfection. It has acclimated to the inrush of the Emperor's power, evolving into a higher form. A successful experiment at last!"
Rey's expression remained unreadable as he eyed the abomination. "You call that thing perfection? It's nothing more than a monstrosity."
Dr. Shwartz's eyes narrowed.
"You wouldn't understand. This is the future, the pinnacle of strength and evolution! Now, behold its might!" He extended his hand, barking an order.
"Attack!"
"URUAAAHHHHHH!!!"
The beast roared, the sound reverberating through the cave like a thunderclap.
~WHOOOOOMM!!!~
It charged at Rey with terrifying speed, its claws slicing through the air as it swiped at him.
Rey leaped back, his movements fluid and calculated. He landed on a rocky outcropping, his eyes studying the creature intently.
"Let's see what you've got," he muttered to himself.
The creature didn't disappoint. It unleashed a torrent of fiery breath, the searing flames consuming everything in their path. Rey dodged the attack with ease, flipping into the air as the heat singed the ground where he had stood.
"Hmm. Fire breath," Rey noted. "Just like a Dragon, huh?."
The beast shifted tactics, slamming its massive tail into the ground.
The impact sent shockwaves rippling through the cavern, dislodging rocks and throwing Rey off balance.
The creature lunged, its maw snapping dangerously close to his chest.
Rey twisted midair, narrowly avoiding the attack as he summoned a barrier to shield himself from the debris. His focus never wavered as the beast continued its relentless assault. It unleashed one ability after another—ripping spikes from its tail, summoning bursts of dark energy, and releasing deafening sonic roars.
Rey's smirk grew as he dodged each attack.
"Gotcha," he whispered.
Dr. Shwartz observed from his vantage point, his confidence swelling with every passing second.
"You're outmatched, boy!" he called out, his voice dripping with arrogance. "You're no match for my masterpiece! Give up while you still can!"
Rey ignored the taunt, his mind piecing together the creature's attack patterns. His fingers twitched slightly, the faint glow of his aura intensifying as he activated one of his own skills.
When the beast lunged again, Rey didn't retreat.
Instead, he dashed forward, weaving between its massive claws and striking it with precise blows. Sparks flew as his aura-coated fists connected with the creature's scales, each strike testing its durability.
Dr. Shwartz laughed, his voice echoing with triumph.
"You can't possibly damage it! This is the apex of evolution, far beyond the likes of you!"
But Rey simply smiled. "Who said I was trying to damage it?"
The beast roared again, this time charging up another fiery breath attack. Rey stood his ground, allowing the flames to engulf him. For a moment, it seemed as though he had been consumed.
"Foolish," Dr. Shwartz sneered.
When the flames subsided, Rey stood unharmed, his body coated in a swirling aura that shimmered with an otherworldly glow.
His smirk widened as he looked at the beast.
"Thanks for the lessons. I've learned all your tricks."
Dr. Shwartz froze, his eyes widening in disbelief. "What... what do you mean?"
Rey didn't answer.
Instead, he ascended into the air, his body radiating an immense, overwhelming aura. The energy around him grew denser, layers of power stacking atop one another as he activated the very abilities he had just copied from the monster.
The beast snarled, preparing to attack again, but Rey was faster.
He surged downward like a meteor, his body cloaked in flames, dark energy, and sheer destructive force.
The impact was cataclysmic.
~BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMMMM!!!~
The ground beneath them erupted, a massive crater forming as Rey's strike tore through the beast's body. The creature let out a final, guttural roar before disintegrating into nothingness, its once formidable form reduced to shreds.
The cavern fell silent, save for the sound of crumbling rocks and the faint hum of residual energy.
Rey emerged from the crater, his steps steady and deliberate.
He wiped the dust from his face as he approached Dr. Shwartz, who was on his knees, staring at the devastation with a vacant expression.
"My masterpiece... destroyed..." the scientist muttered, his voice breaking. "This is impossible... You used its power. You... you destroyed it with its own abilities."
Rey stopped in front of him, his gaze cold and unyielding. "Your so-called masterpiece was just another obstacle. Now, you're going to answer my questions."
Dr. Shwartz looked up at him, fear flickering in his eyes. Rey's aura flared again, a silent warning of what would happen if he refused.
'Killing that single creature caused my Levels to shoot up like crazy. If I can keep this up, or find other Monsters like this, Leveling Up would be even faster than I previously thought…'
For that reason—and others, of course—Rey was ready to investigate the shivering man.
'I want to know everything.'

chapters.title: Chapter 933 - 933: Rogue Hero
chapters.content:
The cave was eerily silent after the massive crater and the destruction of the Evolved Monster.
Rey's cold gaze remained locked on Dr. Shwartz, who was trembling, his knees hitting the ground as he mourned his lost masterpiece. The fire of arrogance that once lit his eyes was replaced by sheer despair. Rey stepped closer, his voice cold and cutting.
"Start talking," Rey demanded, his tone brooking no argument. "Who else is involved? Where's the Dragon Emperor's main stronghold? And how far have you gone with this abominable research?"
Dr. Shwartz gulped, his hands shaking as he began to mutter, "The… the Dragon Emperor commands us from the shadows. We only know fragments of his plans… but the experiments here are a mere prelude…" He coughed violently, blood dripping from his mouth. "We… we were promised power… dominion over… over…"
Suddenly, his words were cut off as his eyes bulged.
Blood began seeping from every orifice—his nose, his ears, even the corners of his eyes. Rey's instincts screamed at him, and he leaped back, immediately erecting a barrier of glowing energy around himself.
Dr. Shwartz let out a horrific scream as his body contorted unnaturally.
His flesh bubbled and swelled grotesquely, and within moments, he exploded in a violent burst of gore and dark energy. The shockwave slammed against Rey's barrier, cracks spiderwebbing across it before the force dissipated.
Lowering his shield, Rey's sharp eyes scanned the scene, only to see something monstrous emerging from the carnage.
Where Dr. Shwartz had once stood was now a towering, deformed figure.
Scales rippled across its body, shimmering in dark, iridescent hues. Its limbs were elongated and clawed, and its face was a horrifying blend of human and dragon, with glowing crimson eyes that radiated mindless rage. Spiked wings jutted out from its back, torn and malformed, twitching spasmodically as the creature let out a guttural roar.
Rey frowned, his mind racing.
"So, you had the formula in you all along," he muttered. "And it activated because you were a traitor to the Dragon Emperor. I guess you didn't see that coming, huh?"
The Dragonoid's roar grew louder, and it charged at Rey with terrifying speed.
Despite its grotesque appearance, it possessed incredible brute strength.
Its massive claws swiped at him, the sheer force of the attack sending shockwaves through the cave. Rey dodged nimbly, flipping backward and landing gracefully on a rocky outcrop.
"No Skills, no strategy… just raw power," Rey observed. He smirked. "Looks like you're all brawn and no brain. That makes this easier."
The Dragonoid lunged again, its claws smashing into the outcrop and shattering it into rubble. Rey leaped into the air, summoning a sword with a flick of his wrist. The blade gleamed with a dark aura as he activated [Battle Aura], enhancing his physical and magical capabilities.
The fight was brief but brutal. The Dragonoid's attacks were relentless, its movements erratic and wild. But Rey's combat prowess far surpassed its mindless aggression. Each swing of his sword was precise, each dodge calculated. He danced around the creature, striking at its joints and weak points, slowly wearing it down.
His [Grand Weapon Mastery] ensured that every attack hit with maximum efficiency.
Finally, as the Dragonoid lunged at him one last time, Rey sidestepped and drove his sword through its chest. The creature let out a bloodcurdling shriek, thrashing wildly as dark energy erupted from its body.
With a final burst of power, Rey unleashed a devastating explosion of magic, reducing the Dragonoid to ash.
Panting lightly, Rey landed gracefully on the ground, dismissing his sword. He stared at the pile of ash and smoldering remains, his mind heavy with disappointment.
"So much for getting answers," he muttered. "This was just a dead end."
Rey clenched his fists, frustration bubbling within him.
"If Tess or the others had been the ones investigating, the same thing would've happened," he reasoned. "These cultists are too devoted to the Dragon Emperor. Even in death, they're just pawns."
He sighed deeply, running a hand through his hair.
There was no point dwelling on it now. The mission was over, and there was nothing left for him here. Turning toward the cave's entrance, he activated his Flight Spell and ascended into the sky, the cool night air brushing against his face.
As he soared back toward the Base, Rey's thoughts drifted.
This encounter had only solidified his resolve. The cult, the experiments, the Dragon Emperor… they all needed to be stopped. And if the others weren't willing to take decisive action, he would do it alone.
The stars twinkled above him as he flew, their light a stark contrast to the darkness he had just witnessed. Rey's expression hardened, determination burning in his eyes.
"One way or another," he vowed silently, "I'll put an end to this madness."
********
[A Few Days Later]
In the dimly lit chamber, the air was thick with tension.
The circular room, concealed deep within the heart of an unknown fortress, exuded an aura of secrecy and menace. Around the table sat a collection of shadowy figures, their faces obscured by masks and hoods.
Each of them represented a facet of power, from military might to covert espionage, all united under the banner of the Dragon Emperor's will.
At the center of the room, a man dressed in a sharp, dark suit stood with a sleek tablet in hand. The soft glow from the device illuminated his face, revealing a cold, calculating expression.
Behind him, a large projection flickered on the wall, showing surveillance footage of a base engulfed in chaos.
The footage played out in silence, save for the occasional hum of static. Bodies of Monsters and researchers lay strewn about, evidence of a ferocious battle. Flames licked the edges of the structure, and debris scattered the area.
The only clue to the perpetrator was a shadowy figure moving at inhuman speed, their face frustratingly blurred.
The man with the tablet turned to the group, his tone calm but edged with accusation.
"This base was cleared in one night," he said. "All research destroyed. Every operative was eliminated. The surveillance footage was nearly useless, and the energy signatures left behind scrambled much of our technology."
He tapped his tablet, freezing the image on the blurry silhouette. "This is the only visual evidence we have. And yet, the agreement was for The Resistance to carry out investigations only—not this."
He turned his sharp gaze toward a man seated at the far end of the circle.
The figure wore a plain robe, his hands folded in front of him, the faint light glinting off a chain around his neck.
The others turned their attention to him as well.
"The assignment was given to one of the most reliable Squads within The Resistance," the seated man said, his voice steady but defensive. "I don't know what went wrong. They always deliver, and they know their parameters."
"Then explain this," the man with the tablet snapped, gesturing to the carnage on the projection. "We throw bones at The Resistance in order to keep the members occupied and distracted while we execute the Emperor's larger plans. Nothing more. We cannot afford loose cannons!"
The robed man clenched his fists.
"I swear to you, I will look into this. I will rein them in."
"You'd better." The man with the tablet's voice dropped to a menacing whisper. "Your use to the Emperor is to keep The Resistance under control. That is your role. If you truly want to rise to the Inner Circle, you must prove your worth. Do not forget that."
The robed man bowed his head, his voice firm but laced with submission. "I understand. It will not happen again."
The other figures in the circle murmured their assent, a ripple of agreement passing through the room.
The man with the tablet turned back to the projection and zoomed in on the shadowy figure. The image remained frustratingly blurred, the figure's energy distorting the recording. Despite this, their movements were fluid and efficient, a deadly precision that sent chills down the spines of even the most hardened individuals in the room.
"We have no name, no face, no allegiance," the man said, his tone heavy with frustration. "But we know this: whoever this is, they are dangerous. Their interference threatens everything we are building. We must identify them—immediately."
A woman with a sharp voice spoke from another side of the circle. "Could this be a rogue? Perhaps someone acting outside their jurisdiction?"
"Possible," the man admitted, his finger tracing the blurred outline on the tablet. "But their energy signature is unlike any recorded member of The Resistance. It's volatile, disruptive… and their skill level is incredibly high too."
The robed man lifted his head slightly. "I will have The Resistance dedicate resources to finding this individual. Whoever they are, they will not elude us for long."
"Good," the man with the tablet said. "And remember: failure is not an option. If this person interferes again, it will not only be your head on the line but all of ours. The Emperor does not tolerate mistakes."
A tense silence fell over the room as the projection faded, leaving the chamber cloaked in shadow once more. One by one, the figures in the circle stood and departed, their movements silent and deliberate.
The robed man lingered for a moment, staring at the empty space where the projection had been.
His fists tightened, his thoughts a swirling mix of anger and fear. He could not fail—not now, not when he was so close to securing his place in the Emperor's Inner Circle.
"Whoever you are," he muttered under his breath, "I will find you. And I will make you pay."
The chamber doors closed behind him, sealing the room in darkness once more.

chapters.title: Chapter 934 - 934: Departure For HQ
chapters.content:
'I wonder what's going to happen now?'
Rey leaned against the wall, arms crossed, as Tess stood at the center of the room, her commanding presence drawing every eye.
The dim light of the Resistance base cast long shadows, but her expression was clear: this wasn't a discussion.
"We've been ordered to return to Headquarters," she announced, her voice firm but carrying a note of resignation. "The higher-ups are concerned about the destruction of the base we were sent to investigate. They want us out of this region immediately."
Josh, seated at the edge of the table, frowned and leaned forward.
"Why? We had nothing to do with that. We followed orders, inspected the place, and reported back. Why should we run like we're guilty of something?"
Tess let out a soft sigh, rubbing her temples.
"I know, Josh. I've made the same argument. But the higher-ups believe it's too dangerous to stay here. They think the Dragon Emperor's forces might launch a sweep of the entire area, looking for whoever was responsible. If we're caught in their crossfire, there's no telling what could happen. Retreating to HQ is the safest move."
Rey, leaning in the shadowed corner, stayed silent at first, his mind replaying the events of the past night. He knew why the base had been destroyed and who was responsible. But admitting that now would only complicate things.
He straightened up and fixed his gaze on Tess.
"When do we leave?"
"Immediately," Tess said. "We have an hour to pack everything and meet at the entrance. Everyone needs to be ready by then."
The room fell into a brief silence, each member digesting the news. Finally, Andrew stood, breaking the tension. "Understood. We'll be ready," he said, his calm demeanor diffusing some of the unease.
"Good," Tess replied, her tone softening slightly. "This isn't ideal, but it's what's been decided. Dismissed. Get your things and prepare to move."
The group disbanded, some heading for their quarters, others for the storage rooms.
Rey walked with measured steps toward his room, thoughts swirling.
He had been meticulous the night before, ensuring no direct traces of his involvement would be found. But the aftermath still weighed heavily on him. The sight of the five humans transforming into grotesque Monsters and Dr. Shwartz's twisted fate lingered in his mind.
Inside his room, Rey began gathering his belongings.
His travel bag was sparse, containing only essential gear and a few personal items.
He moved with efficiency, but his mind was elsewhere.
'Why now?' he thought. 'Why did they order us to pull out so soon? Are they really this afraid of the Dragon Emperor, or is there something else they're not telling us?'
He slung the bag over his shoulder and checked his weapons, making sure they were secured but accessible. After a moment's hesitation, he reached for the enchanted dagger he'd taken from one of the enemies he had fought.
Its faint hum of power was a reminder of the chaos he had caused.
Rey glanced at the clock.
He still had time, but lingering in his room wouldn't do him any good. With a final sweep of the space, he left, heading toward the base's entrance.
Most of the team was already there when he arrived. Dexter and Andrew were double-checking their equipment, while Josh leaned against a pillar, arms folded, looking less than pleased. Mia was securing a satchel of documents, her movements precise and methodical.
Tess stood near the exit, her posture tense as she reviewed a small data pad.
"All set?" Tess asked as Rey approached.
He nodded. "Ready."
Within the next few minutes, the entire team had gathered, their bags packed and weapons at the ready. Tess looked over the group, her gaze lingering on each member as if silently counting them.
"Good," she said. "Once we're out of the base, we'll take the standard route to the extraction point. HQ will have transport waiting for us there. Stay sharp and stick together. Let's move."
The team fell into formation, with Tess leading and Andrew taking the rear. The base's hidden entrance opened with a low rumble, revealing the dense forest that surrounded their location.
They stepped out into the cool night air, their movements silent and coordinated.
Rey kept to the middle of the group, his senses on high alert. His thoughts, however, were conflicted. Returning to HQ felt like a step backward, a retreat from the questions he wanted answered.
The Dragon Emperor's forces, the experiments, the cult—it all felt too important to leave unresolved.
But for now, he had no choice but to follow Tess's lead. As the team disappeared into the forest, Rey cast one last glance over his shoulder at the base that had been their home for quite some time already.
'I would have had to leave eventually, and this presents me with quite the opportunity… even if it is abrupt.'
He had always been curious about the Resistance's HQ, and now he would see it for himself.
'I guess I might see my older brother again… what a pain.'
"Listen up," Tess began, her voice firm but low. "We're heading to HQ via a secure route. At the first checkpoint, we'll pick up a hidden vehicle. From there, we'll drive to another checkpoint where we'll switch to a hovercraft. That'll take us the rest of the way. I expect everyone to stay alert and follow orders. No deviations."
Josh shifted his bag onto his shoulder. "Why all the cloak-and-dagger stuff? HQ afraid the Dragon Emperor's people will tail us?"
"It's a precaution," Tess replied, her eyes narrowing slightly. "We're not taking any chances. The destruction of that base has stirred things up, and we can't afford to be sloppy."
Rey kept silent, though his mind lingered on everything being said.
The group departed swiftly, their steps silent as they created even more distance from their base.
After trekking through a narrow forest trail for about thirty minutes, they reached the first checkpoint. Hidden behind a thick grove of trees was a concealed hatch.
Tess crouched, entering a series of codes into the keypad beside it.
With a quiet hiss, the hatch slid open, revealing a sleek, black vehicle with reinforced plating.
"Our ride," Tess said, gesturing for everyone to get in.
Josh whistled softly. "Didn't know we had toys like this stashed around."
"HQ plans for contingencies," Tess replied curtly. "Now get in."
The team quickly loaded their bags into the vehicle and climbed aboard. Tess took the driver's seat, while Andrew sat beside her to monitor the navigation system. The rest of the team settled in the back, with Rey sitting near a window, his eyes scanning their surroundings.
The vehicle's engine purred quietly as Tess started it.
They rolled out, following a barely discernible path that cut through the dense forest. The drive was tense but uneventful. The team spoke little, each person lost in their thoughts. Rey occasionally glanced out the window, noting how the trees grew thinner as they approached the next checkpoint.
After about two hours, they arrived at a nondescript clearing.
Waiting for them was a sleek hovercraft, its metallic surface gleaming faintly under the sunlight. Tess parked the vehicle and stepped out, gesturing for the others to follow.
"Switching rides," she said. "Load up quickly."
The team moved efficiently, transferring their gear to the hovercraft. Tess approached the control panel of the hovercraft, activating it with a special key card. The craft hummed to life, its turbines glowing faintly.
"This thing is a beauty," Dexter remarked, running a hand along the edge of the craft. "Wonder how fast it goes."
"Fast enough," Tess replied. "Now get in."
The thing was large enough to contain all eleven of them, no problem, so they had no issue fitting inside. Once everyone was aboard, Tess took the pilot's seat, and the hovercraft lifted off smoothly.
The transition from the ground vehicle to the air felt seamless.
As they ascended, the sprawling landscape unfolded below them. Forests stretched endlessly, occasionally broken by rivers and patches of open land. Despite the beauty, the team remained focused, aware of the dangers that could lurk anywhere.
Andrew monitored the GPS, occasionally giving Tess directions. "We're on track. Another three hours and we'll be there."
"Good," Tess said. "Let me know if anything changes."
The journey continued in silence.
Rey leaned back, watching the horizon. His thoughts wandered to the events at the destroyed base and the people who had been experimenting on Monsters. He wondered how many other hidden operations like that existed and how far the Dragon Emperor's influence truly spread.
Eventually, the hovercraft's GPS directed them toward a mountain range that loomed in the distance. The peaks were shrouded in mist, and the terrain became increasingly rugged. Tess guided the hovercraft lower, navigating through narrow valleys and over jagged cliffs.
"There it is," Tess said, pointing ahead.
Nestled against the side of one of the largest mountains was a concealed entrance, almost invisible against the rocky surface. Tess expertly maneuvered the hovercraft toward it, landing smoothly on a hidden platform.
As the team disembarked, Tess turned to them.
"Welcome to HQ."
*
*
*
[A/N]
Happy New Year, everyone!!!
I hope you enjoy your day as much as you enjoy these chapters!
