The goal was to build a powerful stronghold in the Eastern Continent as they prepared themselves to fight against the Fairy King. They could use the abundant resources of the Continent and all the infrastructure already available to support their military forces in readiness for the inevitable war.
As this was happening, Rey would be achieving his goals of getting stronger.
"I'll require both of your assistance in my training." Rey said, looking at Ater and The Oracle.
They both nodded in agreement.
"The Fairy King will also assist me greatly, and I won't step out of seclusion until I've reached my goal."
"What goal is that?" Ater asked, curious.
He smiled.
"Max Level."
"Well, that's quite ambitious." The Oracle said with a smile. "But it's doable."
Rey snapped his fingers and a large Magic Circle instantly appeared beneath the feet of all three of them.
"Let's head back first."

chapters.title: Chapter 974 - 974: Seclusion
chapters.content:
[A Month Later]
Nearly a year had passed in the Fairy World since Rey went into seclusion.
All the cogs were moving at lightning speed, as everyone trained daily and never slacked in their preparations for what was to come. During this period of seclusion, The Oracle, Ater, and even the Fairy King were stuck with Rey in seclusion.
In order to forcibly let him reach his full potential in the shortest time possible, the three made a collaborative effort to train him. They also desired that he reached a certain level of mastery over his Primeval Skills.
After all, he now possessed them.
While this was happening, however, a new problem was brewing on the surface.
"Urgent news, Interim Leader!"
A group of Dwarves scurried into a palace and knelt before the person who had been left in charge of everyone for the time being. She was the strongest among the remaining members of the Alliance.
—Fae, Herald of the End.
"What is it this time? Are we being invaded?" She asked lackadaisically, boredom clearly written all over her face.
Despite holding the most powerful role in the Alliance, she was bored out of her mind.
There was practically nothing to do.
'Everyone is performing their roles perfectly well. Both within the Fairy Kingdom and outside it, everything is going smoothly… so there really isn't much to do.'
Fae wished there would be some invasion, or some kind of battle that would let her flex some of her fighting muscles. She was born to fight, and it was her dream to fall in the most glorious battle ever.
Why would she be stuck in such an administrative role.
It seemed the heavens had heard her inner wishes and decided to provide her with exactly what she desired. After all—
"Yes! Invading forces are nearing the shore of the Eastern Continent!" One Dwarf said in worry.
The moment she heard this, Fae jumped in the air.
"F-for real?!"
She tried to suppress the excitement on her face to no avail.
'No… no, I shouldn't be too excited.' She chided herself. 'If the invading forces are lightweight, it wouldn't be worth celebrating.'
In order to be sure that this was the real deal, Fae required more information.
"How many? How many are there?"
The second Dwarf hurriedly spoke. "About a few hundred thousand… but that isn't the most frightening thing about them."
"Oh?" Fae was initially disappointed by the numbers, but the last words the Dwarves uttered piqued her interest.
"What's the most frightening thing?"
"They look like Dragons."
"Undead Dragons? What else is new…" Fae nearly dismissed their worries, waving her hand to casually say it wasn't that big a deal.
However—
"T-they… they're not Undead." The Dwarves responded in a mumble. "They're living creatures with no trace of Miasma on them."
"E-eh?"
This was a strange development that even she didn't know how to process.
"A few hundred thousand Dragons are coming to attack… that sounds pretty serious." Now that she thought it through, her body began to tremble in excitement.
However, once again, she was met with another bombshell.
"They're not Dragons… they just resemble them." The Dwarves sighed in correction.
Fae became confused at this point.
"If they're not Dragons, what are they?" She snapped impatiently. "Are there any other races that look like Dragons in H'Trae."
"N-no… which is exactly our worry."
From what they understood, most of the Dragons had already been wiped out during Rey's battle with the Emperor, with their corpses turned into Undead. Whatever few Dragons remained would never be able to survive a Miasma-filled continent, which was what the Northern Continent was at the present.
A lot of changes had descended on H'Trae after all of this happened, but never before had anyone seen the ones who were currently invading.
"I believe it is best if Interim Leader sees things for herself." The Dwarves finally agreed, urging her to proceed to the outpost in order to observe the situation personally.
"Fine." Fae sighed. "I have nothing better to do anyway."
Time in the Fairy Kingdom moved about ten times faster than in the Outside World at the moment, which meant a month outside was about ten within the Fairy Kingdom. As such, the few minutes that had been spent on conversation with Fae was only equivalent to a few seconds expended in the Eastern Continent.
The invading forces would not have gotten too close.
"Let's go."
Fae and the Dwarves then proceeded to leave the Kingdom, and once they exited its barriers, they teleported to the outpost.
Rather unfortunately, due to the time dilation process, teleportation directly from the Kingdom to the outside world was impossible. It couldn't be done, which was why they had to leave the Fairy Kingdom before such a move could be made.
~VWUUSH!~
Once the group arrived at the outpost, Fae was able to use her enhanced vision to see the swarm of enemies that were rapidly closing in on the Eastern Continent. Just making a rough estimate, they were about three hundred thousand—perhaps slightly more.
However, the most peculiar thing about this invading force was their peculiar appearance.
They had draconic scales on their bodies, with horns that were twisted all over their heads. They had very twisted-looking wings, with some having three or four wings rather than the usual two. Some also had multiple tails or more limbs than normal.
Apart from their incredibly unique features that resembled Dragons, they also had distinct appearances that seemed inspired by the various Races in H'Trae.
Some of these draconic entities were massive like Giants, while some were as stout as Dwarves.
Most appeared humanoid.
They moved in a completely organized unit, led by something that seemed like a higher kind of Dragon—a Draconic Dragon.
It had several wings on its back, three tails, and at least eight limbs. Its gnarled horns and disfigured face made it look like an abomination, but its multiple eyes shone with intelligence and immense cruelty.
Most importantly, it was very strong.
Fae detailedly observed this group in seconds, instantly realizing how dire the situation was.
"It seems Adrien has begun his full-blown invasion, huh?" She muttered, analyzing the fighting force of the enemy.
Tightly gripping her chest to control the excitement that squirmed within her, Fae gave her orders.
"Evacuate the village, engage all defenses, and prepare… for war!"

chapters.title: Chapter 975 - 975: Divine Emergence
chapters.content:
Just as Fae suspected… the situation was serious.
Firstly, the defensive measures of the Eastern Continent consisted of three major layers. The initial and outward one was a massive barrier.
It disrupted the Mana or Miasma of anyone that entered its range, causing Skills and Magic abilities to get distorted. However, not only was the effect minimal on the invading creatures, but it almost seemed like it had no effect at all.
This seemed impossible to all the observers, since every creature either relied on Mana or Miasma to function.
Secondly, the middle layer of the defensive measures was an energy barrier that blocked out the enemy from advancing any further. However, this was unable to stop their march either. Their presence disrupted the function of the barrier, almost as if they were living personifications of the first barrier's effect.
They were able to easily bypass the energy dome, reaching the third and final lie of defense.
—Machines!
Several automatons and remotely piloted weapons of mass destruction intercepted the army of Pseudo-Dragons, creating the very first challenge the invaders experienced since they launched their assaults.
This forced them to slow down their advancement and display their combat prowess.
And… they were powerful!
Not only were these Pseudo-Dragons incredibly skilled at combat, but their control over energy and the variety of Skills they had in their arsenal was beyond amazing.
It was superb!
They seemed to have the superior abilities of Dragons mixed in with the specialty of other races.
Against the defense of machines, they were nearly unstoppable.
The hundreds of thousands of machines were reduced into nothing but scraps. While they did eliminate some of the enemy's forces, it wasn't nearly enough to be considered a worthy trade-off.
By the time the Pseudo-Dragons broke through the third layer of defensive, there were still well over two hundred thousand enemies left.
The situation was brutal, and a full-on battle seemed inevitable.
"Get ready, everyone!"
Fae yelled and raised her weapon, now completely garbed in her battle armor.
Behind her were hundreds of thousands of soldiers, all of them arranged according to their Races, areas of specialty, and method of contribution to the battle. The Fairies had been preparing for war all their lives, so they were masters at battle formations.
As a result, just by watching the Pseudo-Dragons for a few minutes, Fae could already tell the most effective method that would work on them.
The strongest fighters had to be at the forefront, rather than fodder.
They would get support from long-range buffers and assaulters, while constant restraints and defensive measures would be enacted by their forces. It was like throwing pebbles at a mountain, but even weaklings had their uses.
They were best preserved for long-range assaults than throwing their lives away like fodder.
Ultimately, the battle formation was impromptu and the soldiers present didn't constitute of the entire Alliance military might. However, Fae reasoned this would be sufficient in dealing with their current opponents.
'I estimate about a hundred thousand of us will perish here, but since there's still very little we know about the enemy, that number could double.'
However, one thing was certain to her.
'We're going to win!'
Sure, there would be sacrifices, but who among the present soldiers didn't know this?
They chose to stand on the battlefield despite the risk to their lives because they believed in the greater good and desired to bring about change—even if it would be built upon the foundation of their flesh and blood.
Or… they were simple battle-hungry like Fae.
"On your mark…" Fae raised her weapon once more, her eyes fixated on the fast-advancing enemy.
She narrowed her gaze, feeling the palpitation of her racing heart.
"… Get ready…"
The time had finally come—her debut in the battle of the end was here at long last and she could not wait to taste the sweet nectar of war.
Right as she was able to say "Charge," a sudden voice stopped her.
"Stand down."
The voice sounded familiar, and it was filled with so much warmth and firmness that it made Fae nearly burst out in annoyance. A confusing mix of love, admiration, and utter disgust combined in her mind as she thought of the person whose voice she heard in her mind.
"You old geezer…"
The Fairy King was finally out of seclusion, which also meant…
"Wow! You really gathered everyone in such an effective formation." Ater appeared in front of the crowd.
"I'm impressed, Fae."
"R-really?!" Fae's disgust vanished as soon as Ater said this to her.
She truly admired Ater.
He was, after all, the only one who had bested her in battle before. He was also very charming and had such a way with words that it was impossible not to like him after getting to know him very well.
However, his appearance in the battlefield suggested that he too had come out of seclusion.
"What pests." The Oracle's serene voice echoed as she materialized from thin air. "They actually dared to invade this sacred land."
Despite the fact that she had already seen this future before it happened through [Clairvoyance], it still irked her to witness it happen before her very eyes. Despite her personal thoughts on the matter, however, she kept a stoic gaze.
Her emotionless face remained constant.
"Where is the old geezer?" Fae turned to ask both Ater and the Oracle. "And… where is the Champion?"
Personally, she didn't have such high thoughts about Rey.
Sure, he was the destined one who possessed [Doppel], but he was too weak for her to properly respect. The only reason she depicted the level of reverence that she showed him was due to the efforts of Ater, his Familiar.
She reckoned this was the same for other Fairies, since they were all wired nearly the same way.
However, all of that was soon about to change.
"The Fairy King is resting in his palace, and Rey is about to come out, so you don't need to worry." Ater smiled. "The only reason we're here is to enjoy the show."
Fae heard this and raised her brows in confusion.
"Don't we need all hands on deck to ensure smooth victory and prevent unnecessary deaths?"
Her logical side appeared, questioning the rationale behind their forces being so fragmented, as well as the relaxed demeanor of Ater and The Oracle when the enemy's forces were fast approaching.
Even though they were very strong and their addition to the battlefield would make a lot of difference, without the right plan and formation, a lot of people would still die.
"Pfft!" Ater chuckled. "I think you're misunderstanding something."
He then pointed to the far sky, where the enemies had stained as though they were several dots in a clear canvas.
"There's no need for you to be so concerned. Master is going to handle all of them."
"W-what?!"
Fae had never seen Rey in action, so she couldn't believe this.
However, the second she was about to express her doubts in the matter, a sudden beam of light exploded from behind her.
"H-huh? That's—!" She turned back and saw a pillar of light ascending from within the wall of trees; where the Fairy Kingdom was located.
'His energy is leaking outside? How?!'
Before she could process this thought, the light suddenly vanished and an entity appeared above the battlefield, floating in the sky in order to intercept the invading forces.
He was garbed in a pure white robe, his hair dancing white as he looked ahead with purpose.
"A-ahh…" Fae couldn't help but shiver at the sight of this person.
It was Rey, but not the one she used to know.
She instinctively knew that this person had long surpassed the power that she wielded and now existed in the same level as the deities of H'Trae.
The Fairy King… The Oracle… The Dragon Emperor…
… And now, Rey Skylar.
'Looks like today isn't my debut, after all.'

chapters.title: Chapter 976 - 976: Ultimate Singularity
chapters.content:
"Hmm…"
Rey stood in the sky, feeling the breeze and wonders of the world as he fell into deep thought.
He could see everything—feel everything.
"Is this what it feels like?" He smiled, monitoring his Status Window. "To be Divine."
STATUS WINDOW]
- Name: Rey Skylar.
- Race: Human (Otherworlder)
- Class: Ultimate Singularity (SS-Tier)
- Level: 999 (99.99% EXP)
- Life Force: 999,999 000
- Mana Level: 999,999
- Combat Ability: 999,999
- Stat Points: 0
- Skills (Exclusive): [Doppel]
- Skills (Non-Exclusive): [Perfect Singularity]. [Mass Effect]. [Ultimate Ray].
- Alignment: Chaotic Evil
[Additional Information]
You must perish, Rey Skylar… you and your world!
[End Of Information]
He was bursting with power, and even his [Doppel] was already ninety percent filled up at this point. He had all kinds of Skills within, including three Primeval Skills.
It was undoubtedly the case that he was currently the most powerful entity in H'Trae.
The training he had with Ater, The Oracle, and The Fairy King seemed to have gone on for eons.
He had to constantly Level Up while understanding the depths of their power. Due to how much the Fairy King had to accelerate time, he had gotten incredibly exhausted… which was why he had to rest at the moment.
After finally reaching the cap in his Level at S Class, he had to reach SS Class to attain a new level of power. To do this, he fulfilled tons of conditions, including winning a fight against The Oracle and the Fairy King separately.
Afterward, he had to fight against Ater and push him to the point of death so that his true self would emerge and bestow [Alter] to him. This true self only possessed a mere fragment of Ater's true consciousness and memories, so Rey was unable to obtain all the answers he desired from him.
Still, with this process, he had gotten much stronger.
And now…
"Let's take out the trash first."
… He could now properly call himself this world's champion.
Stretching out his hands casually, his gaze calm and his aim perfect, he spoke softly.
"[Ultimate Ray]."
~BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!!!~
The pulse of multi-colored light that simply coalesced and gave off the illusion of pure white was sent in the direction of the Pseudo-Dragons, completely destroying their existence the moment the energy made contact with them.
In seconds, they were completely eliminated.
Afterwards, he snapped his fingers and activated another Skill in his arsenal.
"[Perfect Singularity]."
Instantly, all the devastated layers of defense was rebuilt—or rather, restored—to the way they were prior to the invasion. However, considering how insufficient the layers were, he proceeded to improve them with his next Skill.
"[Mass Effect]."
Instantly enacting his will on the island-wide layers of defense, he imbued them with his own energy and altered their functions so they would properly adhere to his specifications.
"The next time the enemy tries to break into this, they'll meet a wall of existence erasure.'
Rey wondered how they'd get through.
'Knowing Adrien, though… he already has something planned.' A wry smile formed on his face as he cast his perfect gaze ahead, allowing himself to see so many futures and details that he was previously incapable of.
However, once his sight reached the Northern Continent, it went dark.
'He's interfering with the System… with the Skills I have… and also with the overall powers in H'Trae.' Rey reasoned. 'It's why the previous barriers didn't work on the enemy until I improved them.'
Despite the fact that Rey had already reached the pinnacle of existence in H'Trae, it still wasn't sufficient. This could only mean one thing.
"He's using powers beyond H'Trae.'
That was dangerous, no matter how Rey looked at it. The longer they spent on the defensive, the more initiative Adrien would have in enacting his grand scheme.
'He must be stopped before then.'
At this point, there was no reason to delay the grand war any longer. Rey already knew the army that Adrien sent was nowhere close to his overall force. It was simply a probe to test the powers that existed in the Eastern Continent.
'And now that I've announced my presence to the world, he must already know I'm back.'
That meant there was no going back.
'With all the pieces gathered, the time has come for our final confrontation.'
*********
[Meanwhile…]
"Huuu…"
Adrien stood still, both hands placed behind him as he stared at a massive mechanical structure that was covered in a large Magic Circle. The machine hummed, creating distortions all around, but it hardly bothered him at all.
Unlike before, his form had completely changed from how it used to be.
His pitch black hair was longer, and the whites in his eyes had grown black. His irises had an ominous purple glow in them, and his pale skin was crawling with dark energy, while also being covered by a slime-like substance.
This slime communicated telepathically to him now, and it was laughing.
"I feel it! I feel my beloved Master's return!"
This was Emil, and the moment she felt Rey's energy shoot out from the Eastern Continent, she couldn't stop rejoicing. Adrien was tempted to shut her up, but instead he let her ramblings fuel his determination even further.
"He came earlier than expected, which means I have to make some alterations in the plan again."
He had already noticed something was off when the Eastern Continent was recaptured about a month ago, which was why he sent all the failed experiments to attack the place as some kind of probe.
'The fact that they've all died shows how powerful the enemy has become.'
They had gotten more powerful than he accounted for.
'I've run out of time.' Adrien frowned slightly. 'Which means I will have to stall, even if it means using the last of my forces to buy me sufficient time to complete this project.'
His eyes shone the moment he looked at the machine.
This was it!
His goal was nearing fruition, and it made his heart race in excitement despite his calm demeanor.
Emil noticed all of this, since she was bound to him, and she laughed once again.
"My true Master is coming for me! Master is going to defeat you and cause your downfall!"
Adrien chuckled upon hearing this.
"If I fall, you do too…" Upon uttering those words, the slime fell into silence. "Besides, I don't think I'll lose to Rey."
Their history had proven time and time again that he was always one step ahead.
'I've always won and will always win.'
He wasn't compromising this status quo for anything less.
"Besides… I still have my trump card to use against him." Adrien smiled, leaving the machine as he slowly walked to another room where a complicated mechanism stood.
There were several pods connected to a much larger mechanism, and within all of those pods were entities whose identities were difficult to decipher.
However, at the center was a familiar face.
Adrien kept both of his hands in his pocket this time as he looked at the largest pod containing a woman who was wrapped with the most intense of energies.
It was Lucielle, currently unconscious as she was trapped in the pod, with a massive Magic Circle enveloping the ground beneath all of them.
A wide grin formed on Adrien's face.
"Let them all come… I'll be expecting you, Rey."

chapters.title: Chapter 977 - 977: Final War Begins
chapters.content:
"We are heading off to war this very instant."
Rey stood at the forefront of the Eastern Continent's shore, his gaze on all the members present in the meeting. Every single important figure was watching him as he addressed them: Ater, The Oracle, the Fairy King's hologram, the representative of each Race, the Otherworlders, the Adventurers Guildmaster, and finally Fae.
The latter was the most excited after hearing the news, her wings fluttering in delight.
"Based on my analysis, we possess exactly 3,891,344 forces in our army. This accounts for all the Undead you have in stock, and every single soldier in the battalions you have gathered."
Everyone nodded, some displaying shock that Rey was able to count their exact numbers in a mere instant. This wouldn't have shocked them if they knew just how far he had transcended the bounds of normal.
He was the ultimate life form of H'Trae at the moment.
"That is sufficient." He added. "We still do not know how massive the enemy's forces are, but that is inconsequential. It is riskier to wait, and more optimal to strike now."
Using the power of [Clairvoyance], Rey already narrowed down the location of [Reset] to the Northern Continent; the same place that Adrien was located. Whether he was the one with [Reset] or not, it was optimal that they struck to obtain the Primeval Skill.
'[Reset] and [Skill Creation] are both in our enemy's territory, so we have every incentive to attack.' He reasoned. 'Plus, now that Adrien knows I'm around, he'll try his best to speed up his plan and create more obstacles for me.'
In order to prevent that from happening, they had to act now.
"We'll send all our Undead forces as a probe and gauge the enemy's power. Afterwards, we'll attack." Rey revealed.
"But, the Undead make up a third of our overall forces." Justin spoke up quickly. "Is it really wise to use up so many as probes?"
He and Belle were the ones in charge of the Undead in his absence, so they knew how vital the forces were. Wasting them as the advance squad made them a little squeamish.
"It is necessary for us to get rid of them." Rey sighed. "Their Miasma would get in the way of our overall forces. In the end, we are living beings and they are Undead, Miasma and Mana can not fully work together."
The army had to be separated either way.
"However, rather than sacrifice our own troops, it's better to send expendable units to battle first. If we choose a small number, we won't be able to fully probe Adrien's strength, which is why need to attack in bulk."
Everyone instantly understood Rey's intentions once he clarified his plan.
"Adrien also has the ability to control Undead, and we have no idea how much his power has grown. In the circumstance that he can hijack our control over those Undead, it's best we do not attack at the same time they do."
In the worst case scenario, Ater could cause their self-destruction since he possessed ownership of their Soul.
"That way, even if it's a loss to us, the enemy will have no access to our forces."
Everyone nodded.
"I am confident that they won't be hijacked, though." Ater added. "Adrien is indeed impressive, but I reckon he still has a long way to go before he reaches my level."
"Perhaps if you used Ancient MajiK, but… you used your Skills on those Undead, right?"
"Yeah… fair enough."
Rey cast his gaze on the enemy continent and his brows furrowed.
"Whatever Adrien is up to gives me a bad feeling. He's always been a step ahead and he definitely has trump cards. However, I can't let that scare me. What we have to do is obvious, so let's all take the risks involved and fight!"
Rey was ready to fight for this world with everything he had.
"YEAHHHH!!!"
So was everyone else.
The troops assembled, and in the blink of an eye, Rey transported the entire Eastern Continent away from its previous position.
~VWUUUUUUSSSSSSHHHH!!!~
It was uprooted from the waters, rapidly ascending into the air as a floating fortress.
This fortress was swiftly teleported away from the East, traveling due north at unfathomable speeds. The sheer mass of the continent, and the amount of power required to move it, was immeasurable to most people.
But Rey was more than able to achieve this feat.
'Using [Mass Effect] to affect the entire Continent, and controlling it with my other Skills, I can control it.'
This made the continent itself a weapon.
'And now… for the initial strike.'
Rey already knew that Ater had hidden his stockpile of Undead in various locations, so he opened a gate in all of those areas and caused the miasma-filled troops to rush out as they organized themselves atop the ocean.
The wide ocean seemed to turn into solid ground as the million Undead troops made formations, dividing their ranks based on expertise and level of power.
With Ater as their commander, they established their formation in no time.
"A-Amazing!" Even Fae was impressed by Ater's skill in generating formations. As a Fairy who spend millennia learning about all kinds of battle formations, his ability in swiftly organizing his army in the most appropriate positions was stellar.
She was once again impressed by Ater.
"Get ready to move out!" Rey's loud voice caused the entire battlefield to quake as everyone watched in sheer reverence as he gave commands.
In the past, Fae had very little to say about Rey, not respecting him at all.
But now?
"He truly is amazing! The most amazing entity in this world."
She completely acknowledged him.
"War is about to begin, everyone… so brace yourself."
The troops marched ahead, with the Eastern Continent floating in the air, as they neared the completely dark Northern Continent.
Rumbles of intense energy caused everything to shake, and everyone could feel the intense pangs of nervousness assail their bodies.
However, they stood strong.
"Incoming troops! Enemy has sent incoming troops!"
As if thinking the exact same thing as Rey, Adrien sent his own Undead army forward, their numbers double the size of Rey's, while also consisting of multiple Dragons—many of whom were Generals.
Each wing was led by the Undead Dragon Lords, with Generals commanding battalions under them. It was an incredibly sophisticated formation, with quantity and quality exceeding Ater's army.
However, Ater's smile only broadened upon seeing this.
"Do you think you can break through their ranks and exterminate this wave?" Rey asked him, unable to see the future due to two main reasons.
One was that [Clairvoyance] was being affected by this world being cut off from the System, hence it could only be used in small bursts at a time and wasn't entirely accurate. As for the second reason, it was the interference being generated from the Northern Continent.
The closer they got to the place, the more Rey could feel his Skills being affected.
As a result, he needed Ater's frank response to be certain of their current situation: would they encounter a loss in this round?
"It's going to be a little tough, considering the sheer mass of his army."
"But would you lose?"
Ater shook his head as he commanded his army to charge forward.
"I'd win!"

chapters.title: Chapter 978 - 978: War Of The End [Pt 1]
chapters.content:
VWUUUSSHHH!!!
The battlefield churned like a storm of death and destruction.
Ater's forces, a massive legion of Undead, surged forward across the blackened ocean, meeting Adrien's overwhelming horde head-on. The air trembled with the reverberations of clashing metal, the screeches of twisted creatures, and the eerie howls of the damned.
Adrien's army was colossal, far larger than Ater's, and included numerous Dragons—terrifying behemoths of decayed flesh and cursed bones. The Undead Dragon Lords led entire squadrons, their presence radiating an oppressive aura that weakened the morale of lesser soldiers. Their dark magic pulsed through the sky, weaving into deadly beams that rained destruction upon Ater's army.
But Ater remained unfazed.
His red eyes gleamed with the calm precision of a grandmaster in the midst of a game.
"Break their ranks into segments. We will divide and conquer." His voice rang through the minds of every single Undead under his control. With expert synchronization, Ater's army restructured its formation mid-battle.
Instead of engaging Adrien's superior forces in a full frontal assault, Ater implemented a layered attack. The weakest skeletons and lesser Undead swarmed forward first, acting as disposable fodder to absorb the initial impact. Behind them, elite Death Knights and Wraiths flanked both sides, moving in a crescent formation to encircle Adrien's forces.
BOOM!
A colossal explosion erupted as a Dragon Lord unleashed a wave of corrupted flames, incinerating hundreds of Ater's weaker troops. But that was expected.
Ater smirked. 'You've fallen for it.'
He sent a mental command, and at once, his Wraiths—beings of cursed energy—swept into action. They phased through the battlefield, bypassing the frontlines and launching surprise attacks deep into enemy formations. Their spectral claws tore through the cursed flesh of Adrien's Dragons, disrupting their spellcasting and coordination. The moment of hesitation allowed Ater's Death Knights to engage the distracted Dragon Lords in direct combat.
The result was immediate.
Several of Adrien's Dragons, overwhelmed by Ater's cunning tactics, screeched in pain as their wings were severed mid-air, sending them crashing into the sea of Undead below, where they were torn apart by thousands of skeletal warriors.
Adrien's generals noticed the shift in battle and quickly restructured their army. They relied on brute force, funneling their forces into the strongest frontal push imaginable, using raw numbers and sheer destructive magic to trample Ater's comparatively smaller army.
But Ater had anticipated this.
He let them advance, then executed his next phase.
"Trigger the trap."
The moment those words echoed through the battlefield, hidden magical circles that Ater had secretly planted during the battle erupted across the battlefield.
Gigantic glyphs of necrotic energy lit up the sky and ground, forming an intricate network of hexes. These magical constructs pulsed with black energy before detonating simultaneously, releasing torrents of deathly energy.
Adrien's frontlines were annihilated in seconds. Tens of thousands of his Undead were disintegrated, their souls ripped apart by the overwhelming necrotic surge.
The explosions also created pockets of void, breaking Adrien's overwhelming numbers into isolated clusters. With the enemy army divided and panicked, Ater's forces moved in for the kill, strategically surrounding the stranded groups and executing them with ruthless precision.
From the sky, a massive skeletal dragon—one of Adrien's personal creations—let out a deafening roar and descended toward Ater, its gargantuan claws glowing with cursed flames. It aimed to rip Ater apart in a single devastating strike.
Ater merely chuckled, his form vanishing just before impact.
The next moment, he reappeared above the dragon, a wicked grin playing on his lips. "You're not the first, and you won't be the last."
With a snap of his fingers, black chains materialized from the void and wrapped around the dragon's entire body, locking its movement. The monstrous beast thrashed violently, but it was futile.
Then, Ater clenched his fist.
The chains tightened, cracking bones, tearing flesh, and causing the dragon to release an ear-splitting howl of agony before being completely crushed into dust.
Adrien's forces faltered. The moment their Dragon Lords began falling, their coordinated advance fell into chaos. Their previous unstoppable momentum turned into a slow, stumbling retreat as Ater's superior tactics and unshakable control dictated the flow of battle.
The Undead army of Adrien, which had once doubled Ater's in size, was now being obliterated at an alarming rate.
And Ater was only getting started.
"Finish them," Ater commanded.
His army surged forward with newfound aggression, executing the enemy with ruthless efficiency. The balance had completely shifted. Adrien's Undead, despite their superior numbers at the start, were now being overrun, their ranks crumbling under Ater's absolute mastery.
The first battle was won.
***************
"Hm…"
From above, Rey watched everything unfold. A satisfied grin spread across his face as he saw Ater's flawless execution of strategy. The first phase of their assault had been a complete success.
Now, it was time for the next.
His gaze lifted toward the colossal barrier that surrounded Adrien's empire. A deep, impenetrable black dome loomed over the land, pulsating with immense energy. It was a barrier infused with Adrien's magic, reinforced by layers of anti-intrusion spells and sealing formations.
A normal army would never break through it.
But Rey was no ordinary force.
He lifted his hand, and golden light surged from his body. Energy rippled through the sky, causing the clouds to part as an overwhelming presence filled the air. Every single soldier—friend and foe alike—turned to look at him, their bodies trembling in awe.
Then, Rey extended his hand toward the barrier.
"[Ultimate Ray]."
A blinding, celestial beam erupted from his palm, thick as a mountain and faster than thought. The sheer pressure of its activation alone sent shockwaves across the land. The beam collided with Adrien's barrier with unimaginable force.
For a moment, the world held its breath.
Then—
BOOOOOOOOM!!!
The barrier shattered into a billion fragments, each piece dissolving into nothingness. The entire empire of Adrien lay exposed.
Rey lowered his hand, his expression calm but resolute. His golden eyes burned with the flames of war.
"Everyone… attack!"
The entire army roared in response, charging forward with relentless fury. The final battle had begun.
Rey, however, had a different objective.
As the battlefield descended into complete chaos, he shot forward at speeds faster than light, heading straight for the massive tower at the heart of the empire.
Adrien was waiting for him.
And Rey had every intention of facing him head-on.
*
*
*
[A/N]
Thanks for reading, and sorry for the delay.
I'm back!
An Extra's POV ends next month, and I'm glad to be here to finish it.

chapters.title: Chapter 979 - 979: War Of The End [Pt 2]
chapters.content:
The shattered remains of the barrier still crackled with dark energy, dissipating into the air like dying embers.
The entire Northern Continent had been cloaked in its protective shell moments ago, but now it was gone—obliterated by Rey's Ultimate Ray. And yet, as he stepped into the heart of the enemy's domain, he barely spared the destruction a thought.
The tower loomed before him, a colossal construct of black metal and twisting obsidian, stretching toward the heavens like a spear meant to pierce the sky itself. From the outside, it was an ominous monument of darkness, but Rey knew the true defenses lay within.
He strode forward.
The moment his foot crossed the entrance, the air vibrated. Walls shifted, runes ignited, and a cascade of alarms blared through the tower.
[Security protocols activated].
Chains of red energy lashed out from the walls, seeking to bind him. Gigantic mechanical constructs emerged from the floors and ceilings, each wielding massive cleavers infused with nullification energy—designed to sever any form of power they came into contact with.
Hundreds of sentinels appeared from the shadows, their bodies forged from an unknown metal that shimmered with an otherworldly glow. Their eyes locked onto Rey, their weapons gleaming as they lunged toward him in unison.
A normal being—no, even an army of elite warriors—would have struggled against these defenses.
Rey did not.
His body blurred.
A single step, and the very air cracked.
The chains disintegrated before they could reach him. The towering constructs crumbled, their cores obliterated before their weapons could even be swung. The sentinels—formidable in every aspect—didn't even realize they were dead until their bodies split apart, severed by an invisible force.
He didn't need to fight. He didn't need to strategize.
He overpowered everything.
His sheer presence broke the defenses meant to hold an entire invasion force at bay.
And then, he was at the top.
The grand hall was vast, stretching endlessly in all directions. Black marble lined the floors, reflecting the eerie violet glow that emanated from the walls. Floating sigils carved into the very fabric of reality hummed with energy, and at the center of it all—standing behind an impenetrable wall of darkness—was Adrien.
Rey's eyes locked onto him.
Adrien appeared slightly different from what he remembered. His black hair had become long, framing his sharp features, his eyes pools of pure darkness with a faint glimmer of violet shifting within them. Shadows coiled around his body, rising and falling like living creatures, giving him an almost spectral appearance.
But there was something different about him.
Something… wrong.
Rey took a step forward. The dark barrier stood between them, thick and unyielding, its presence more suffocating than the one that had covered the entire continent.
This was stronger.
Adrien smiled. "Took you long enough."
Rey didn't return the sentiment. His golden gaze bore into Adrien's, his voice steady.
"It's time now, Adrien. Whatever you have planned, I'm ending it now."
Adrien let out a soft chuckle, shaking his head. "Do you really think you understand anything? Even now, after all this time?"
"You betrayed H'Trae, you betrayed me…" Rey's tone was sharp, cutting through the air like a blade. "You let this world fall into chaos just to achieve whatever twisted plan you've concocted."
There were a lot of things in Rey's mind, and a lot more to express, but there was no point in saying them at this moment. All he knew for sure was the resolve etched in his heart, and the determination to save this world which he loved so much.
"I'll never forgive you."
Adrien's expression remained unreadable. "And what would you have done, Rey? Stood by and watched? Played the hero? Clung to your morality while the real players moved their pieces?"
'How much does he know about the ones above?' Rey reasoned to himself, his fists clenched.
No, this was no time for speculation.
Just action!
"I wouldn't have sacrificed so many lives."
Adrien exhaled slowly, his eyes narrowing. "You think too small. You always have."
Rey didn't respond. He simply moved.
He struck the barrier with his full might. The entire hall shook, the walls quaking as cracks spread across the dark energy. The sheer impact sent a wave of force surging through the tower, causing distant structures to groan under the pressure.
For a moment, the barrier held.
Then—
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMMM!!!
It shattered!
The explosion of dark energy illuminated the entire tower, sending shockwaves rippling outward. Rey lunged through the fading remnants of the barrier, his hand closing around Adrien's throat before the man could even react.
He lifted him effortlessly, golden eyes glowing with sheer power. "Where is your real body?"
Adrien merely smirked, despite the crushing force around his throat.
"Who knows?"
Rey's grip tightened, but before he could press further, Adrien's smirk widened. "You came all this way thinking it was just me?"
Rey's eyes narrowed. "What are you talking about?"
Adrien's fingers snapped.
And then—
A presence.
Rey felt it before he saw it.
A titanic pressure descended upon the hall, warping the air with its sheer weight. A sensation that Rey had only encountered once before in his life.
'Dragon Emperor?!'
He turned.
At the furthest end of the hall, a figure emerged.
His breath hitched.
White hair cascaded down in endless waves, reaching the ground like strands of silk. Nine horns curved from her head, dark cracks splitting her otherwise flawless skin. A floating crown hovered above her head, shifting with an eerie glow.
Her eyes.
Deep black, marked with fractures of red light, like something that had been shattered and hastily pieced back together. The dark markings on her body pulsed, and behind her, multiple wings unfurled—an unnatural mix of holy radiance and abyssal corruption.
A tail lashed behind her, shifting between solid form and shadow.
Rey's entire body froze.
This wasn't the Dragon Emperor… at least, not the one he knew.
"…Lucielle."
She stepped forward, her gaze empty, yet piercing.
Adrien chuckled from within Rey's grasp. "She's my trump card."
Rey slowly released Adrien, his focus entirely on the woman before him. His mind raced, piecing together what he was seeing.
Lucielle was powerful—impressively so. But this… this was something else.
This wasn't just her.
Something had been done to her.
Adrien dusted himself off, stepping back casually. "You thought you were prepared, Rey. But you don't even understand what's really at play here."
Rey took a step forward, every fiber of his being screaming that something was horribly wrong.
His golden eyes flashed with appraisal, and that was when he saw it.
Her Status Window.
[STATUS WINDOW]
- Name: Luci'elle
- Race: Dragon Royal (Transcendent)
- Class: Dragon Emperor (SS-Tier)
- Level: 999 (Max)
- Life Force: 999,999
- Mana Level: 999,9999
- Combat Ability: 999,999
- Stat Points: 0
- Skills (Exclusive): [Reset]
- Skills (Non-Exclusive): [World Destruction]. [All Magic]. [Perfect Domain]. [Complete Dominion]. [Evil Personified].
- Alignment: Chaotic Evil
[Additional Information]
The destroyer of the world, and herald of the will of chaos. She is the ultimate enemy of H'Trae, and the absolute deity of the Dragons.
This vile entity and you shall bring about the end of this world.
[End Of Information]
"I see…" His voice was steady, but his chest tightened. "So the [Reset] Skill was with you all along?"
She didn't answer.
Instead, her wings spread wide, the black fractures in her eyes gleaming.
Adrien grinned. "Well then, shall we begin?"
The temperature dropped.
The hall darkened.
And Lucielle moved.
*
*
*
[A/N]
I have a new novel, everyone!
It's called Arcane Era, and it's on Webnovel at the moment. I hope you'll check it out now, or at least when you're done with this novel. It's definitely better than An Extra's POV, and I don't say that lightly.
Thanks for reading.

chapters.title: Chapter 980 - 980: Rey Vs Lucielle
chapters.content:
The instant Lucielle emerged, Rey knew this fight would be unlike any other.
Her pure white hair cascaded to the ground, an eerie contrast to the dark markings that twisted around her face and arms. Her nine horns curved elegantly, a floating crown of darkness hovering above her head. Her wings—multiple and vast—spread wide, crackling with raw, uncontrolled power. Her tail swayed behind her, a monstrous appendage despite her humanoid form.
And her eyes… black voids with glowing crimson—as if they devoured light itself.
This was not the Lucielle he once knew.
The air itself warped, tremors ripping through reality as her presence threatened to collapse the entire tower.
Yet Rey did not hesitate.
As soon as she moved, her hand a blur of annihilation, Rey grabbed Adrien's clone and threw it into her attack.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMM!!!
A blinding explosion of energy erupted as the clone disintegrated instantly, erased without resistance.
But Rey was already moving.
He lunged, his body blurring through space as he closed the distance, his hand glowing with the immense power of [Ultimate Ray].
Lucielle met him mid-air, her pale fingers twisting reality as she unleashed a blast of pure destruction—a collision of magic, concept, and devastation.
They clashed.
Another roaring eruption resounded, causing the dark metallic ground beneath them to shatter—turning into whatever was less than dust in an instant. The walls soon followed, until the entire structure began to experience rapid deterioration and structural collapse.
In barely a second—
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMMMM!!!
The entire tower exploded, obliterated in the wake of their battle as they broke into the open sky.
Below, the battle raged on, Rey's army of Fairies, Elves, Humans, Dwarves, and Giants fighting against Adrien's Dragonoid-hybrids, mutated beings with scaled flesh, wings, and draconic power.
But none of that mattered now.
The Northern Continent itself trembled as Rey and Lucielle tore through the atmosphere, their every strike warping reality and sending shockwaves that devastated the land beneath them.
Lucielle's wings flapped once, and the sky shattered like glass, creating void fissures that sucked in everything nearby.
She raised her hand.
[World Destruction].
A black sun materialized above her palm, a celestial body of ruin, pulsating with pure annihilation.
Rey reacted instantly.
He twisted his body mid-air, activating [Mass Effect], extending his influence around him so it covered the entire area of impact. Once he was done, he glared at the dark orb being generated, shifting the gravity around him to warp away from the attack—but Lucielle had already anticipated it.
With a flicker of [Perfect Domain], space folded around Rey, trapping him in a sealed battlefield where her destructive magic was absolute.
Rey's eyes narrowed.
She was fast.
She was strong.
And—most of all—she had lost herself to the power she now wielded.
He vanished in an instant, using a Skill in [Doppel] to split into multiple versions of himself, each one attacking with different SS-Class Skills.
Lucielle countered with inhuman precision, her mastery of [All Magic] allowing her to conjure every possible defensive and offensive spell simultaneously.
It was a battle of pure supremacy, their movements too fast for the eye to follow, their attacks tearing through dimensions, each strike shaking the very foundations of existence.
For every wound Rey inflicted, Lucielle used [Reset], rewinding reality to undo the damage.
He crushed her ribs—they healed instantly.
He severed her arm—it restored itself before it could even hit the ground.
He unleashed [Ultimate Ray], obliterating her upper body—she rewound time and returned to perfect form.
'We have equal Stats, and the battle will continue to drag on endlessly because of her [Reset] if I don't do something different…'
Right as he was having this thought, Lucielle attacked again, her spear of condensed destruction aiming straight for Rey's heart.
But this time—
He let it hit.
The world twisted.
Time rewound.
Rey felt the skill activating, saw the flow of causality unraveling as Lucielle's [Reset] rewrote the event.
He had already copied it.
'It's practically impossible for the Dragon Emperor to die in H'Trae—not just because of [Reset], but also [Evil Personified].' A flash of understanding filled his eyes as he narrowed them on the entity before him.
As calm as his analysis was, he could feel his heart bleed just from staring at her.
'Not fair… this isn't fair…' He thought within himself. 'I was powerless to stop Alicia from dying… I had to let Esme go as well, and now…'
He fought back the feelings of hesitation that wrapped themselves around him—coiling around his heart as he stared at the lost and completely transfigured Lucielle.
"... Do I have to let you perish too?"
WHOOOOSH!
Lucielle lunged at him with an even greater attack—several times more devastating than the previous ones—but her next strike never landed.
Rey's hand caught her wrist mid-motion, his fingers tightening like an unbreakable vice.
Her glowing eyes widened in shock.
For the first time—she hesitated.
Rey stared at her.
He had no more reason to drag this out.
He could end it now.
She had become a monstrous force of destruction, far beyond salvation.
Killing her would be easy.
His hand tightened around her throat.
He raised his other hand, energy gathering, forming a series of patterns using the SSS-Class Skills at his disposal which were surely powerful enough to erase her completely.
She had to die.
He knew that.
But then—
Lucielle's lips curled into a twisted, sorrowful smile.
'W-what…?!' His eyes widened as he saw this—witnessing a glimpse of the woman he once knew within the monster he held.
And then, right before he could fully comprehend this sight—
ZZZTTTTZZZZ!!!
—She self-destructed.
VWUUUUUUUMMMMMMMMM!!!
The world screamed.
Her body erupted in an explosion of apocalyptic energy, a detonation so vast that it threatened to consume the entire Northern Continent.
The battlefield shook violently, both Rey's and Adrien's forces staggering under the sheer force of the destruction.
Everything was about to be erased.
Rey's expression hardened.
This had to stop.
He had to make his choice—right here, right now.
Below him were hundreds of thousands of people who were risking it all to save this world—to reach a better future for H'Trae. Lucielle was strong enough to destroy everything they had worked so hard for, which meant he had to stop her.
There was no choice.
'I have to do it… I have to end this.'
He moved faster than light, his body piercing through the flames, reaching Lucielle's core—the epicenter of her detonation.
His hand shot forward.
And he stabbed her through the heart.
Lucielle's glowing black eyes widened, her body jerking violently as Rey drew her in close, his forehead pressing against hers.
A golden glow surrounded them, an overwhelming force pulling them away from reality—
"[Domain of Man]..." He muttered, activating his Skill.
Everything shifted.
The battlefield, the continent, the war—all of it vanished.
They entered a different plane, an alternate dimension crafted by Rey's overwhelming power.
Lucielle's breath hitched, her fingers weakly gripping his wrist.
For the first time in the fight, her eyes cleared, her voice barely above a whisper.
"R-Rey?"
"Lucielle…"
He closed his eyes, his grip firm but not cruel.
Then, as her consciousness faded into the depths of the abyss, his voice solemnly echoed in the vast—empty space.
"... I'm going to save you."

chapters.title: Chapter 981 - 981: Within The Void
chapters.content:
Death.
What does it truly mean?
By definition, it occurs when one ceases the constant act of breathing and the heart stops beating.
However, what happens during this process? What takes place after?
Rey mulled on these thoughts as he stood in the Domain Of Man, staring at Lucielle's lifeless body which was in his grasp. He had killed her before she could use [Reset], using his own version of the Skill to counteract her own.
Plus, the effects of [Evil Personified] were null in his domain, since it existed in a separate dimension from H'Trae.
In other words… she was truly dead.
Or was she?
'I could give up now.' Rey told himself. 'I could stop this and chase after Adrien.'
After all, he had already sacrificed enough for the cause. He had given up on finding true happiness in his comrades—many of which would undoubtedly perish in this war—and had simply chosen to focus on the task.
But…
'You're the only one left…' He looked at Lucielle's body, watching as it crumbled to dust in his arms. The white fragments danced around him, dissipating like smoke.
'... The only one left that I…'
Closing his eyes and inhaling softly, he controlled his emotions.
He remained that way for a few seconds, slowly opening it to reveal his golden eyes. And so, as his white hair fluttered in the darkness, he exhaled deeply and clenched his fists in both resolve and unwavering determination.
He had decided!
"I won't let you die… not you!"
How was he going to achieve this? By definition, she was already dead.
Based on the laws of H'Trae, time flowed in a linear fashion—like a story that was being told. Affecting the past was nigh impossible as a result of this concept, as one could only march forward as the story unfolded.
He couldn't physically travel to the past to save her, just as he couldn't travel to kill Adrien.
He had to find a solution in the present.
Rey thought for a moment, and he finally found the only route to take.
To begin, he called upon a Skill.
"[Clairvoyance]."
Using this SSS Tier Skill, he could peer into the past, present, and future… as long as he possessed sufficient storage. Peering into the future was compromised, since the world's connection to the System was rapidly eroding and the path it was heading in had deviated from its intended destination.
However, Rey could still see into the present as well as the past.
He chose his answer instantly.
'I will see through your past, Lucielle… from the moment you were conceived to your death!'
And so he began.
Rey witnessed Lucielle's birth, he saw her take her first walk, how she said her first word, and how she grew from a toddler to a slightly older child. He kept watching her in the void of space, present in all that she experienced in her lifetime.
He was there when she discovered her affinity for Magic, and was witness to her rise in the United Human Alliance—from a nobody to a powerful Mage.
As much as he watched her good memories, he was privy to the bad ones.
Yes, he witnessed her make breakthroughs in Magic… but he also saw how devastated she became when she got news of her sister perishing in the war. He witnessed her descent into madness and her rise from the clutches of insanity. He saw how she was used, and how she used others.
He witnessed her glorious rise… and then her tragic downfall.
'After Adrien sent me to Earth, he captured her and ran all sorts of experiments on her… perfectly fusing more Draconic Mana into her while brainwashing her thoroughly with Skills and altering her body chemistry.' Rey saw it all.
Of course, she resisted the Skill strongly.
Since her body was in temporal stasis thanks to her transformation into a younger version of herself, and then the mutation she induced on that body to become a Dragon, she had all sorts of resistance to Adrien's power.
But, ultimately, she lost the intense battle and succumbed to his power.
It was torture to watch, but Rey witnessed Lucielle's transformation into the most powerful Dragon in H'Trae… which was how she managed to awaken the Dragon Emperor's Skills and became Adrien's trump card.
Then, he revisited her battle with him; watching how she lifelessly attacked him...
… And how he killed her.
"With this, I now have all the information and memories about the one known as Lucielle."
Rey retrieved all of the memories he retrieved from [Clairvoyance] and condensed it to form a warbling orb. After he was done, he smiled at the completion of the first task.
"Now… for the second."
This time, he called upon another SSS Tier Skill.
"Architect."
With this, he could create pretty much anything: organic or inorganic.
He used this power to recreate Lucielle's body—every nook and cranny—missing no single detail. He completely reconstructed her Dragon Emperor body, once again laying eyes upon the grotesque entity she had become.
However, he wasn't stopping there.
Once he was done, her naked body stood right opposite him, and a small smile formed on his face.
The second phase was complete.
"For the third… [Alter]."
He used this Skill to completely transform the body before him—perfectly undoing the brainwashing effects and corruption that her body had endured. He strengthened her form and removed the weaknesses present therein.
He reverted her tainted appearance and restored her purity.
The long silver-white hair, her crimson eyes, and the clear pale face that seemed to belong to an angel—she had all of those features once again.
The Lucielle before him—while still being a Dragon Emperor-level entity—was as beautiful as he remembered her. She still had all her Skills and Class, but she was devoid of the blighted effects of Adrien's forceful mutation.
"And now… it's time for the fourth phase." Rey directed the condensed orb of memories to enter into Lucielle—forming a core for her soul.
This was the foundation that would make her into a living being.
The entire process thus far had already taken centuries upon centuries, yet they felt infinitesimal in the grand scheme of things.
He had to make no mistakes, and he had to connect every single dot perfectly.
After successfully integrating the artificial soul into the husk that was Lucielle, he proceeded to the fifth and final phase.
"Wake up, Lucielle…" He breathed into her, infusing her with his divine energy.
And then—
"Huu…"
—Her eyes fluttered open as she gave her first breath, completing the march of restoration that he had embarked on.
The first thing she saw within the darkness was light.
And within that light… was Rey Skylar.
"R-Rey…?"
"Yes, Lucielle… it's me." He smiled at her, widening his arms as he expected a hug when she rushed towards him.
However, it wasn't a simple hug he received.
Instead, her lips pressed strongly against his as she clung tightly with him in a passionate embrace.
This moment shattered the Domain Of Man, and the both of them found themselves floating high in the darkened sky—atop the crowd of warring soldiers and beasts.
"Rey… I…" Lucielle, finally realizing her actions, pulled away in hesitance. However, Rey drew her back in and gave her a more passionate kiss—one that paralyzed her entire body.
"You came back…" She whimpered as she held him tight, as if scared he would leave her once again.
Rey smiled as he witnessed this child-like display, but he indulged her as he whispered under his breath:
"Yes… and I'm never leaving you this time."

chapters.title: Chapter 982 - 982: The World Above
chapters.content:
~Master, what's the progress on finding Adrien?~
Ater's voice suddenly echoed within Rey's mind, finally causing him to jerk back into reality. His eyes regained their focus as he returned to the seriousness of the present situation.
This was war.
"I couldn't find him in the tower. He has to be hiding somewhere within H'Trae, so I'll use my [Clairvoyance] to scour the entire world and find him. If I get any kind of interference, I can assume it is him." He said in response.
~But would interference necessarily mean his presence? What if he predicted this and set us up on another wild goose chase?~
"That's true…" Rey rubbed his chin. "Knowing Adrien, he has all sorts of countermeasures to make sure his plans succeed.
There was no telling what layer of his plan they were currently in, but Rey knew full well that they were running out of time.
'We need to stop him before he achieves his grand goal—whatever it is.'
"I think I know where he is." All of a sudden, Lucielle's voice echoed in the air, interrupting Rey's conversation with Ater.
"Really?"
"Yes."
'How does she know it? I went through her memories, but there was no mention of where Adrien is at the moment.'
"I am connected to all the Dragonoids that he created, which means I can detect the energy waves and communication pattern that connects each of them. It's like a web of intricacy spun by Adrien… but at the center is a single source."
Lucielle pointed up and smiled.
Rey raised his head and was dumbfounded for a moment.
Then, his eyes widened and a broad smile formed on his face. He realized what Lucielle meant by merely a single glance, even chiding himself for not recognizing it sooner.
"He's not in H'Trae… he never was." He muttered. "It all makes sense. Something like this suits him the most…"
And that was none other than the void beyond the world of H'Trae.
~He's in outer space?~
"Yes." Rey grinned. "My [Clairvoyance] doesn't extend to anything beyond the confines of this planet, so I would never have found him with that method."
His eyes flashed as he stared at Lucielle, kissing her passionately one more time.
"Thanks a lot for your help."
She giggled upon hear this, blushing violently—even as many people fought to their deaths right below them.
~Master, focus!~
"Yes… I understand! I'm right on it."
"I can come with you to help." Lucielle said excitedly, her broad smile and bright eyes displaying intense energy that could nearly blind anyone.
However, Rey had to reject her offer.
"You should focus on trying to stop the Dragonoids. Since you're connected to them, can you find a way to shut them down? Or, at the very least take control from Adrien?"
"His hold on them is strong… and since they're not fully Dragon, it will be hard."
"But can you do it?"
Lucielle nodded and made a confident grin.
"I can!"
"Perfect! Focus on doing that, and tell me when you're done. What about you, Ater? What are you up to?"
"Trying to find a way to understand what Adrien is planning so I can shut it down." He responded curtly.
"Excellent. I expect great results soon."
~Understood!~
"Hold the fort until I return. If all goes well, I'll be able to stop Adrien very soon!"
Rey highly doubted it would be that easy, but he also wasn't intent on dragging out the war any more than it currently was. He had to end things… fast.
WHOOOOOSH!!!
He ascended high above—darting into the darkened sky like an unstoppable projectile.
Before long, everyone and everything beneath him became small and insignificant. He no longer heard the cries of the battlefield, and he no longer felt the chaos that was being wrought in the Northern Continent.
Before long, he could see all the lands of the world, and every bit of its oceans.
However, he never stopped ascending.
—Not until he finally reached it.
"So this is where you've been hiding…" Rey smiled as he looked at a round, dull sphere that orbited the world beneath him.
The moon of H'Trae.
Ignoring the vastness of the space around him, including the glimmering stars that shone in the distance, Rey charged straight for the moon.
The entire thing was Adrien's domain.
And by penetrating it, venturing straight into the massive structure, he found himself inside the world that Adrien had created for himself.
—An empty space filled with nothing but a towering construct.
It was a machine of unparalleled complexity. Words could not explain the intricacies of the object, as it was connected with all kinds of wires and mechanical objects. All sorts of Mana Crystals, gems, and essences decorated its outer shell.
And its inner walls warbled with power.
Within the shell of the moon, this machine took up an incredible amount of space—about ten percent.
The rest was occupied by a lone figure who stood before it.
"Adrien." Rey said as he stared at the boy before him.
"Rey… you've surprised me. I didn't think you'd get here so quickly." Adrien said, expressing genuine surprise while staring at Rey.
'The moon certainly had barriers, but it wasn't difficult to get past them. But why are there no other security measures? It's just him that's present here… well, other than that thing.' Rey stared at the machine behind Adrien, noticing an immensely powerful and complicated barrier surrounding it.
Even for someone like him, it would take a little while to destroy the entire walls of power.
'I should get started…' As Rey took a step forward, Adrien raised his hand and urged him to stop.
"I know what you're trying to do, but just listen to what I have to say first." Adrien said calmly. "The device is in its final stages, and a very unstable wormhole is being created within it at the moment. If you do anything to destabilize it, you could end up creating a singularity strong enough to delete this entire universe."
Rey knew he wasn't lying.
The amount of energy he sensed from within the machine was too much—even for him.
Still, he moved forward.
"If you let it succeed, it is a wormhole that connects multiple other worlds—and I don't mean just Earth, but all the worlds that exist in this fabricated multiverse. Don't you want to see? I plan to connect myself to all of those other worlds that exist, Rey!" Adrien's eyes were wide open as he spoke, almost as if he was a child. "This world is too boring! It's too predictable! And just as I expected, there are some hands pulling the strings from the shadows."
'He's talking about the Administrators like Seraph and her superiors…'
"Nothing in this world matters, Rey! They're all just… we are all just puppets on strings! It's all meaningless… at least not unless we ascend to the higher reality where something actually matters!"
For the first time since the speech began, Rey halted his steps and said something to Adrien.
"Is that your plan? To sort through all the worlds that exist until you find a crack that leads you to the world above? The realm beyond this one… beyond the power of the System or the control of the Administrators…"
"S-so you know!" Adrien's eyes widened. "Then why try and stop me—?"
"Because… I have had a glimpse at what exists high above our world." Rey responded, his tone perfectly calm as his face turned lull.
"... And it is equally as meaningless."

chapters.title: Chapter 983 - 983: Rey Vs Adrien [Pt 1]
chapters.content:
"What do you mean by that?"
Adrien's face instantly changed once Rey concluded his words regarding the world beyond, disregarding it as meaningless. The facade of the one shrouded in darkness refused to accept those words, and his frown grew deeper as a result.
"You don't know what you're talking about." He responded to Rey with a snicker. "Whatever glimpse you saw doesn't justify your conclusion."
Rey shrugged as he advanced further.
"Perhaps… but I certainly know those above do not have our best interests at heart. You realize the only reason you can still use your System is because we found a way to slow down the corrosion of the world."
"Oh? Tell me more about that!"
"You're not listening…" Rey shook his head as he glared at Adrien.
Just as he suspected, talking to this person had no use. Adrien was too manipulative to be trusted, and too obsessed with his goals to be reasoned with. The most optimal route to save the world would be to destroy him.
And—
"I'll make it quick."
—Rey had long resolved to perform this task.
WHOOOSH!
The entire area trembled as Rey made his way to Adrien, shocking the latter with his immense speed. Despite how powerful Adrien had become, he was nowhere near strong enough to stop Rey's march.
BOOOM!
The blow alone caused everything unprotected by the darkness to erupt.
In that single instant, the moon itself exploded—sending shards of its rocky body flying in all directions—some in the direction of the planet beneath it.
Rey noticed this and pulled all of the rocks together, causing them to boil up as they stuck together. He then targeted Adrien, who had been ragdolled towards his machine, and hurled the massive orb of burning intensity at him.
As expected… the damage was catastrophic.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!!!
Rey narrowed his eyes as he looked at Adrien and instantly noticed a detail that wasn't present the last time they fought. Despite his earlier punch and the entire destruction of an energy-charged moon around him, the boy remained completely unharmed.
"Hahaha! Did you think I wouldn't expect your attack at some point? You won't be able to destroy me or my barrier that way." Adrien grinned as he stared at Rey from a distance.
"...."
"I can't be destroyed, and neither can this barrier—not until the task of my machine is complete."
"I see now… so that's what happened."
"Hm?" Adrien cocked his head as darkness swelled around his body, protecting every fraction of it with immense energy.
"Emil… it's been a while." Rey smiled as he looked at Adrien—no, not at him, but the slimy darkness he had hidden beneath the darkness. "I thought you were dead since our connection was severed, but now it makes sense how he isn't receiving any damage."
Emil had infinite durability, and as such, if one could properly cultivate that quality of hers and wear her like a suit, they could protect their bodies from whatever attack that was thrust at them.
'She can even take the power of Ultimate Ray… impressive.'
He had initially thought Adrien used the darkness that shrouded him to protect himself, but it was all to hide Emil. After all, Rey's current 'Ray' could destroy practically anything within H'Trae… even energy.
But Emil wasn't from H'Trae and she also had infinite durability.
In essence, Adrien—who was her new master—had attained virtual indestructibility as a result.
He was invincible.
'Or so he thinks…' Rey charged forward, rushing towards the grinning Adrien.
Before he could react, he grabbed him by the throat and glared deep into his eyes. Then, he caused his entire body to burst in pure white light—eviscerating every fragment of darkness that surrounded Adrien until only the slime suit he wore underneath remained.
"I'm going to strip her from you."
"You can't." Adrien yelled with a laugh. "I've made sure we're permanently bound together."
Rey clutched at Adrien's chest, feeling the resistant slime pushing back against him against its will. Then, he connected deeply to it with his mind.
At that point, he could hear faint sounds coming from within it.
~Master… please… kill me…~
Rey wished he could fulfill Emil's wishes, but all of his Skills were nearly useless against her—especially now that she had matured to this point.
'Even my SSS-Tier Skills cannot affect completely who isn't of H'Trae. With the System's collapse and the world barely hanging together, the rules have gotten a lot looser, so there isn't regulation and Stats to fully exploit when it comes to such an otherworldly entity.'
All of H'Trae's leftover resources were focused on its natives.
And, by specification, Otherwordlers like Rey.
The rest were not particularly beyond the System, but without the strong hold of the System, he wouldn't be able to use [Appraisal] or [Clairvoyance] on them. This was why he didn't notice Emil when he first attacked Adrien, and he couldn't track down Adrien as well.
However, despite all this, Rey didn't give up hope.
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!!!
He tried every destructive Skill at his disposal, aiming for both Adrien and his machine, but both didn't budge in the slightest. As they fought in the vastness of space, high above the the war-ridden H'Trae, Rey swam through the darkness and kept assaulting the far weaker Adrien—finding it impossible to win.
After exhausting all of his conventional options, he decided to create some distance from Adrien, his back turned to H'Trae as he glared at the darkness-covered individual before him.
"Is that it? You've given up already?"
"Something like that." Rey shrugged. "None of my attacks are really going through."
"Hmm… is that so?" Adrien smiled as he gazed at Rey condescendingly. Their relationship over the years had evolved over time, and even he could not have predicted that their interactions would lead to this juncture.
"You should have responded to me back then."
"I don't know what the fuck you're talking about, but… I guess I'll give it my all this time."
All of a sudden, Rey drew both palms together and began to gather all the essences of his destructive Skills. Active and Passive Skills worked together in tandem, and coagulated between both hands as they glimmered with incredible power.
Adrien noticed the sheer intensity of the power being gathered and whistled.
"That's some incredible power. I reckon it would be able to destroy the planet behind you quite easily." He smiled. "But, even something of that scale won't—"
"Emil… I know there's still a lot I have to apologize for. You've been the most amazing Familiar to me, and without you… I never would have made it as far as I have. Remember the fight with The Oracle? Our adventure with the Elves? How you perfectly tricked Adrien and got all those nice Skills like a great Familiar should…"
The moment Rey began to speak, Adrien felt his body slowly shake.
"Hm? This is…?!"
"All this time, you've told me how much you love me… I never said it back despite constantly feeling the same." Rey smiled softly. "Thank you, Emil, for everything you've done… and I love you too."
At this point, Adrien could hear several loud screams in his head—all of them from Emil.
Despite suppressing her, her loud cries continued.
~I LOVE YOU SO MUCH, REYYYYY!!!~
Rey knew she was uttering those words within Adrien, because he simply knew Emil that well.
And it was because of this that he uttered his next and final command to her.
"Please, Emil… die for me."
And, much to Adrien's surprise, happiness filled Emil's heart as she joyfully responded to his cold request.
~AS YOU WITH, REY!~
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMMMMMMMMMM!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 984 - 984: Rey Vs Adrien [Pt 2]
chapters.content:
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMMMMMMMMMM!!!
The incredible energy that Rey had stockpiled throughout his conversation with Emil finally reached breaking point, and he sent everything charging in the stunned Adrien's direction.
"W-what? What are you—?!"
Normally, Adrien would confidently take the attack, certain no harm would come to him.
Now, his face was pale.
The reason could be traced to the bizarre sight taking place right before Rey's eyes. Adrien's body was swelling in multiple directions, with spiky shapes coming out of all sides—as though Emil was attacking him from all angles.
"Are you crazy?! You really want to die? You're going to die because of HIM?!"
Adrien's voice echoed in the void of space as the destructive blast neared both him and Emil. His eyes flashed with horror as he swiftly did his best to erect a dark barrier at the last minute to protect his incredibly unstable body from the attack.
However, the ultimate ray easily tore through his blast and pushed him towards his machine, the intensly concentrated blast finally beginning to eat through all of the seemingly overwhelming resisteance that he had prepared.
"E-Emil, stop! Wait! Please!"
At this point, it was Adrien who pleaded with the Familiar.
Due to the rules of the System applying very loosely to her, she could disobey her new master without consequence. However, due to the both of them being bound, whatever damage Adrien received would be received by Emil.
Perhaps not by her physical body, but her soul would sustain equal damage.
And now that she was intentionally peeling off her layer of protection from Adrien, it meant he was free to receive all the damage he was confident in rejecting.
The result was devastating.
"ARRRGHHHHHHHHHHH!!!" Adrien screamed, feeling his body deconstruct as his barrier all over his machine began to whittle down.
Within a fraction of a second, the entire thing crumbled, and both Adrien and his machine exploded in white fiery light that resembled a supernova. Rey erected a barrier that protected the planet from the radiation and intense heat that the explosion undoubtedly released, his eyes on the collapsing machine and eviscerating Adrien.
Amidst the light was Emil, whose body was now turning to dust since Adrien was dying.
Rey made a sad smile as he looked at her.
'I wish things were different.' A sigh escaped his parted lips. 'I tried to save you.'
However, the case for Emil was too different from Lucielle, so he couldn't properly revive her. He had no choice but to watch her burn in the light, hoping that she felt no pain throughout the entire process.
Then, finally—
FSHUUUUUU…
—The lights dimmed and the explosion fizzled out, returning the world of darkness to its initial state. Rey's eyes narrowed as he looked far into space and found nothing—no trace of Adrien or the machine.
By using an Ultimate Ray that could destroy an entire planet, his goal was to destroy even the spatial anomalies that would cause a black hole to swallow the universe. From the looks of things, he had succeeded.
Hence, there was no Adrien… no machine… and no grand evil plan.
It was over.
'Yet why do I still feel so uneasy?'
Before long, his question would be answered in the form of a shimmering multi-colored blot in the vast darkness of space.
'Hm? What's that?' Rey's eyes narrowed, struggling to comprehend the complexity of the mixtures of light he saw.
He couldn't understand the colors and their combination.
He would have liked to call the colors by name, but their definition eluded him. The colors formed shapes that were foreign to him as well. Some were, of course, familiar to him—as were some colors—but there were also strange ones that made his head churn in ignorance.
Amidst this confusing display, something that had the resemblance of a human being emerged from the expanding blot of confusion.
This humanoid entity made sounds that Rey did not understand.
It spoke in words that he could not comprehend.
Then—
"Can you hear me now? Ah… much better…"
—The glitch subsided, with the shapes and colors stabilizing to form comprehensible concepts that his mind could process. The blot in space was actually a wormhole, filled with a collage of various colors that contrasted so finely with one another.
As for the entity that emerged from swirling gate… it turned out to be none other than a human.
And not just any human.
"Adrien…" Rey frowned as the boy materialized right before his eyes. "So you didn't die."
"Obviously."
Adrien now looked much older than before—having the appearance of a man nearing his forties. His dark hair had turned gray at the sides, and while his eyes had some wrinkles around them, he still maintained a fairly youthful appearance.
His previously naked body soon had clothes on, and he was completely clad in an all-black suit covered in a black cloak.
His all-black eyes focused squarly on Rey and he finally spoke.
"You were foolish to try and stop me. If you had succeeded, everything and everyone in this world would have been trapped in its decaying existence.
